# Page: Overview

# Overview

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

- [omtra/models/omtra.py](omtra/models/omtra.py)
- [omtra/models/self_conditioning.py](omtra/models/self_conditioning.py)

This document provides a high-level introduction to the OMTRA codebase: what it is, what it does, and how the code is organized. For installation and usage instructions, see [Getting Started](#2). For detailed explanations of core concepts, see [Core Concepts](#3). For model architecture details, see [Model Architecture](#4).

## What is OMTRA?

OMTRA (Omni-Task Representation and Assembly) is a multi-task generative model for structure-based drug design. It uses flow matching to generate 3D molecular structures, protein conformations, and pharmacophore features either unconditionally or conditioned on various inputs.

The model is implemented as a PyTorch Lightning module ([omtra/models/omtra.py:55-1053]()) that orchestrates training and sampling across multiple tasks using a shared `VectorField` architecture ([omtra/models/vector_field.py:40-1179]()).

**Sources:** [readme.md:1-21](), [omtra/models/omtra.py:1-86]()

## Core Capabilities

OMTRA supports the following task categories:

| Task Category | Representative Tasks | Code Entity |
|--------------|---------------------|-------------|
| **Unconditional Generation** | Generate novel drug-like molecules | `denovo_ligand_condensed` |
| **Protein-Conditioned Design** | Design ligands for binding sites | `fixed_protein_ligand_denovo_condensed` |
| **Molecular Docking** | Dock ligands into protein structures | `rigid_docking_condensed` |
| **Conformer Generation** | Generate 3D conformations | `ligand_conformer_condensed` |
| **Pharmacophore-Guided Design** | Design molecules matching pharmacophore constraints | `denovo_ligand_from_pharmacophore_condensed` |

Each task is defined by which **modalities** (molecular properties) are fixed as inputs versus generated by the model. See [Tasks and Modalities](#3.1) for details.

**Sources:** [readme.md:7-16](), [readme.md:217-256]()

### Component Responsibilities

| Component | File(s) | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| **OMTRA** | [omtra/models/omtra.py:55-1053]() | Main model class; orchestrates training, conditional path sampling, and inference |
| **VectorField** | [omtra/models/vector_field.py:40-1179]() | GNN architecture that predicts trajectory destinations during flow matching |
| **Task Classes** | [omtra/tasks/tasks.py]() | Define which modalities are fixed vs generated for each task |
| **Modality Classes** | [omtra/tasks/modalities.py]() | Define molecular properties (atom types, positions, bonds, etc.) |
| **Graph Construction** | [omtra/data/graph/]() | Convert molecular data into DGL heterogeneous graphs |
| **Prior Sampling** | [omtra/priors/]() | Initialize generation by sampling from prior distributions |
| **Datasets** | [omtra/dataset/]() | Load training data from Zarr stores |

**Sources:** [omtra/models/omtra.py:55-86](), [omtra/models/vector_field.py:40-76]()

| `configs/` | Hydra configuration files | `config.yaml`, task-specific configs |
| `omtra_pipelines/` | Data processing pipelines | `plinder_dataset/`, `pharmit_dataset/` |

## Data Flow

### Training Pipeline

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Data Loading"
        Zarr["Zarr Store<br/>(chunked arrays)"]
        Dataset["Dataset Class<br/>PlinderDataset/<br/>PharmitDataset"]
        Sampler["MultiTaskSampler<br/>(batch construction)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Graph Construction"
        RawData["Molecular Data<br/>(coords, types, bonds)"]
        BuildGraph["build_complex_graph()<br/>DGL HeteroGraph"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Forward Pass"
        SampleTime["Sample t ~ U(0,1)"]
        CondPath["sample_conditional_path()<br/>(x_t = α_t·x_0 + β_t·x_1)"]
        VFForward["VectorField.forward()<br/>(predict x_1 from x_t)"]
        Loss["Compute Losses<br/>(MSE, CrossEntropy)"]
    end
    
    Zarr --> Dataset
    Dataset --> Sampler
    Sampler --> RawData
    RawData --> BuildGraph
    BuildGraph --> SampleTime
    SampleTime --> CondPath
    CondPath --> VFForward
    VFForward --> Loss
```

**Sources:** [omtra/models/omtra.py:269-322](), [omtra/models/omtra.py:386-517]()

### Sampling Pipeline

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Initialization"
        Task["Task Definition<br/>task_name_to_class()"]
        LoadModel["omtra_from_checkpoint()"]
        SamplePrior["sample_priors()<br/>(x_0 ~ prior)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Integration Loop"
        SetXT["Set x_t = x_0"]
        Predict["VectorField.forward()<br/>(predict x_1)"]
        Step["VectorField.step()<br/>(x_t += dt·vf)"]
        Iterate["Repeat for<br/>n_timesteps"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        Unbatch["dgl.unbatch()"]
        Convert["SampledSystem<br/>(to RDKit/Biotite)"]
        Write["Write SDF/PDB/CIF"]
    end
    
    Task --> LoadModel
    LoadModel --> SamplePrior
    SamplePrior --> SetXT
    SetXT --> Predict
    Predict --> Step
    Step --> Iterate
    Iterate --> Predict
    Iterate --> Unbatch
    Unbatch --> Convert
    Convert --> Write
```

**Sources:** [omtra/models/omtra.py:602-940](), [omtra/models/vector_field.py:778-932]()

## Key Concepts

### Tasks and Modalities

OMTRA's flexibility comes from its **task-modality** system:
- **Tasks** define generation scenarios (e.g., docking, de novo design)
- **Modalities** are molecular properties (e.g., atom positions `lig_x`, atom types `lig_a`, bond orders `lig_e`)
- Each task specifies which modalities are **fixed** (provided as input) vs **generated** (predicted by the model)

For example:
- `rigid_docking_condensed`: fixes protein structure (`prot_x`, `prot_a`) and ligand identity (`lig_a`), generates ligand positions (`lig_x`)
- `denovo_ligand_condensed`: generates all ligand modalities unconditionally

See [Tasks and Modalities](#3.1) for complete details.

**Sources:** [omtra/models/omtra.py:111-113](), [omtra/tasks/tasks.py]()

### Flow Matching

OMTRA uses **flow matching** to gradually transform samples from a prior distribution (t=0) to the data distribution (t=1):

1. Sample a time `t` uniformly from [0, 1]
2. Construct `x_t` via conditional path: `x_t = α_t·x_0 + β_t·x_1`
3. Train `VectorField` to predict `x_1` (the destination)
4. At inference, integrate the learned vector field from t=0 to t=1

The `InterpolantScheduler` ([omtra/models/interpolant_scheduler.py]()) defines the interpolation functions `α_t` and `β_t` for each modality.

See [Flow Matching for Molecules](#3.2) for details.

**Sources:** [omtra/models/omtra.py:542-600](), [omtra/models/vector_field.py:778-932]()

### Heterogeneous Graphs

OMTRA represents molecular systems as **DGL heterogeneous graphs** with multiple node types:
- `lig`: ligand atoms
- `prot_atom`: protein atoms  
- `pharm`: pharmacophore features
- `npnde`: non-polymeric non-drug entity atoms

Edge types connect these nodes spatially (k-NN, radius) and chemically (covalent bonds). The `VectorField` processes these graphs using `HeteroGVPConv` layers that operate on geometric vector features.

See [Graph Representation](#3.3) for details.

**Sources:** [omtra/models/vector_field.py:108-183](), [omtra/data/graph/]()

## Entry Points

### Command-Line Interface

The primary CLI entry point is `routines/sample.py`, which:
1. Loads a checkpoint using `omtra_from_checkpoint()`
2. Prepares input graphs from provided files
3. Calls `OMTRA.sample()` to generate molecules
4. Writes outputs to SDF/PDB/CIF files

The CLI is wrapped by the `omtra` command installed via setup.py.

**Sources:** [readme.md:159-168](), [routines/sample.py]()

### Training Scripts

The training entry point is `routines/train.py`, which:
1. Constructs a `MultiTaskDataModule` from Hydra configs
2. Instantiates the `OMTRA` model
3. Uses PyTorch Lightning `Trainer` for multi-GPU training
4. Saves checkpoints periodically

**Sources:** [readme.md:548-550](), [routines/train.py]()

### Web Application

The web application (`omtra_webapp/`) provides an interactive interface built with Flask/FastAPI. It wraps the same `OMTRA.sample()` method used by the CLI but adds visualization and interactive parameter tuning.

**Sources:** [readme.md:520-544]()

## Model Checkpoints and Inference

Pre-trained model weights are stored in `omtra/trained_models/` and loaded using checkpoint utilities. The CLI automatically selects the appropriate checkpoint based on the `--task` argument, or users can specify one explicitly with `--checkpoint`.

During inference:
1. `omtra_from_checkpoint()` loads the model state
2. The task class determines which modalities to generate
3. Prior distributions are sampled for each generated modality
4. `VectorField.integrate()` performs the flow matching integration
5. Outputs are converted to standard molecular file formats via `SampledSystem`

**Sources:** [readme.md:141-149](), [omtra/models/omtra.py:602-940](), [omtra/eval/system.py]()

# Page: Getting Started

# Getting Started

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [readme.md](readme.md)

</details>



This page provides an overview of how to install, configure, and run OMTRA for the first time. It covers the essential prerequisites, the main workflow from setup to sampling, and a minimal working example. For detailed instructions on specific topics, see the child pages: [Installation and Setup](#2.1), [Command Line Interface](#2.2), and [Quick Start Examples](#2.3).

## Prerequisites

Before installing OMTRA, ensure your system meets the following requirements:

| Requirement | Specification |
|-------------|---------------|
| Operating System | Linux |
| GPU | NVIDIA GPU with CUDA support |
| CUDA Version | CUDA 12.1 recommended |
| Python | Python 3.11 |
| Package Manager | conda or mamba (for manual installation) |
| Docker | Docker + NVIDIA Container Toolkit (for Docker installation) |

**Sources:** [readme.md:47-51]()

## Installation Overview

OMTRA provides two installation methods, each suited to different use cases:

### Installation Methods

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Manual Installation"
        M1["Create conda env<br/>python=3.11"]
        M2["Clone repo"]
        M3["Run build_env.sh"]
        M4["omtra CLI available"]
        
        M1 --> M2
        M2 --> M3
        M3 --> M4
    end
    
    subgraph "Docker Installation"
        D1["Pull gnina/omtra:latest<br/>or build locally"]
        D2["Source docker-cli-setup.sh"]
        D3["omtra CLI available"]
        
        D1 --> D2
        D2 --> D3
    end
    
    M4 -.-> CLI["omtra --task TASK"]
    D3 -.-> CLI
```

| Method | Best For | Key Steps |
|--------|----------|-----------|
| **Manual** | Development, most users | Create conda env → Clone repo → Run `build_env.sh` |
| **Docker** | Deployment, web application | Pull/build image → Source `docker-cli-setup.sh` |

The manual installation ([Installation and Setup](#2.1)) provides direct control over the environment by installing PyTorch, DGL, PyG, and all dependencies through the `build_env.sh` script. The Docker installation encapsulates everything in a container and is particularly useful for the web application interface.

**Sources:** [readme.md:41-138]()

## Key Components

Understanding these core components is essential for working with OMTRA:

### Component Reference Table

| Component | Location | Purpose |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| **`omtra` CLI** | Entry point installed by setup | Command-line interface for all operations |
| **Model Checkpoints** | `omtra/trained_models/` | Pre-trained weights for different tasks |
| **OMTRA Model** | [omtra/models/omtra.py]() | Main generative model class (flow matching) |
| **VectorField** | [omtra/models/vector_field.py]() | GNN architecture for trajectory prediction |
| **Sample Script** | [routines/sample.py]() | Sampling/inference pipeline |
| **DGL HeteroGraph** | Used throughout | Molecular representation with multiple node/edge types |

### Task-to-Checkpoint Mapping

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Tasks"
        T1["denovo_ligand_condensed"]
        T2["fixed_protein_ligand_denovo_condensed"]
        T3["rigid_docking_condensed"]
        T4["ligand_conformer_condensed"]
        T5["denovo_ligand_from_pharmacophore_condensed"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Checkpoints"
        C1["Auto-selected from<br/>omtra/trained_models/"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Files Required"
        F1["None<br/>unconditional"]

        F5["--pharmacophore_file"]
    end
    
    T1 --> C1
    T2 --> C1
    T3 --> C1
    T4 --> C1
    T5 --> C1
    
    T1 -.-> F1
    T2 -.-> F2
    T3 -.-> F3
    T4 -.-> F4
    T5 -.-> F5
```

Each task automatically selects the appropriate checkpoint from `omtra/trained_models/` unless overridden with `--checkpoint`.

**Sources:** [readme.md:141-149](), [readme.md:215-256]()

## Minimal Working Example

Here is a complete minimal workflow to generate your first molecules:

### Step 1: Install OMTRA

**Manual installation:**
```bash
mamba create -n omtra python=3.11
mamba activate omtra
git clone https://github.com/gnina/OMTRA.git
cd OMTRA
chmod +x build_env.sh
./build_env.sh
```

**Docker installation:**
```bash
git clone https://github.com/gnina/OMTRA.git
cd OMTRA
source docker-cli-setup.sh
```

### Step 2: Download Model Weights

```bash
wget -r -np -nH --cut-dirs=3 -R "index.html*" -P omtra/trained_models https://bits.csb.pitt.edu/files/OMTRA/omtra_v0_weights/
```

This creates `omtra/trained_models/` with checkpoint files.

### Step 3: Generate Molecules

**Unconditional generation (no input files needed):**
```bash
omtra --task denovo_ligand_condensed \
  --n_samples 10 \
  --n_timesteps 250 \
  --output_dir outputs/first_generation
```

**Structure-based design (requires protein PDB):**
```bash
omtra --task fixed_protein_ligand_denovo_condensed \
  --protein_file examples/protein.pdb \
  --pocket_center 10.5,20.3,15.2 \
  --bbox_length 23.0 \
  --n_samples 10 \
  --output_dir outputs/sbdd_example
```

**Molecular docking (requires protein and ligand):**
```bash
omtra --task rigid_docking_condensed \
  --protein_file examples/protein.pdb \
  --ligand_file examples/ligand.sdf \
  --n_samples 10 \
  --output_dir outputs/docking_example
```

### Step 4: View Results

Output files are organized in the specified `output_dir`:
- `*.sdf` - Generated ligand structures
- `*.pdb` / `*.cif` - Protein structures (for flexible tasks)
- `*_pharm.xyz` - Pharmacophore features (for pharmacophore tasks)
- `eval_metrics.csv` - Evaluation metrics (if `--metrics` flag used)

**Sources:** [readme.md:53-69](), [readme.md:80-138](), [readme.md:141-149](), [readme.md:259-331]()

## Command Line Interface Overview

The `omtra` command accepts the following argument categories:

### Core Arguments

```bash
omtra --task <TASK> --checkpoint <PATH> --n_samples <N> --n_timesteps <N> --output_dir <DIR>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
|----------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `--task` | Yes | - | Task identifier (see [Available Tasks](#available-tasks)) |
| `--checkpoint` | No | Auto-detected | Path to model checkpoint file |
| `--n_samples` | No | 100 | Number of samples to generate |
| `--n_timesteps` | No | 250 | Integration steps during sampling |
| `--output_dir` | No | None | Directory for output files |

### Input File Arguments

```bash
omtra --task <TASK> --protein_file <PDB> --ligand_file <SDF> --pharmacophore_file <JSON>
```

| Argument | Format | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `--protein_file` | PDB or CIF | Protein structure |
| `--ligand_file` | SDF | Ligand structure |
| `--pharmacophore_file` | JSON, XYZ, or SDF | Pharmacophore constraints |
| `--pocket_ligand` | SDF | Reference ligand for pocket definition |
| `--pocket_center` | `x,y,z` | Pocket center coordinates |
| `--pocket_residues` | `CHAIN:RESID` | Pocket residue specification |

See [Command Line Interface](#2.2) for complete reference and [Quick Start Examples](#2.3) for usage patterns.

**Sources:** [readme.md:159-213]()

## Available Tasks

OMTRA supports multiple drug design tasks through a unified interface:

### Task Categories

| Category | Example Task | Description |
|----------|--------------|-------------|
| **Unconditional** | `denovo_ligand_condensed` | Generate molecules without constraints |
| **Protein-Conditioned** | `fixed_protein_ligand_denovo_condensed` | Design ligands for protein binding sites |
| **Docking** | `rigid_docking_condensed` | Dock known ligands into proteins |
| **Conformer** | `ligand_conformer_condensed` | Generate 3D conformations |
| **Pharmacophore** | `denovo_ligand_from_pharmacophore_condensed` | Design molecules matching pharmacophores |

Each task corresponds to a specific combination of fixed and generated modalities (see [Tasks and Modalities](#3.1)). The task name determines:
- Which modalities are generated vs. fixed
- Which input files are required
- Which checkpoint is loaded (auto-selected)
- Which prior distributions are used

**Sources:** [readme.md:215-256]()

## Common Options

### Ligand Size Control

Control the number of atoms in generated ligands:

```bash
# Use ground truth atom count (for tasks with reference ligands)
omtra --task rigid_docking_condensed --use_gt_n_lig_atoms --n_lig_atom_margin 0.15 ...

# Specify explicit distribution
omtra --task denovo_ligand_condensed --n_lig_atoms_mean 25 --n_lig_atoms_std 5 ...
```

### Stochastic vs Deterministic Sampling

```bash
# Deterministic sampling (default)
omtra --task denovo_ligand_condensed ...

# Stochastic sampling with noise
omtra --task denovo_ligand_condensed --stochastic_sampling --noise_scaler 1.0 ...
```

### Debug Mode

Enable full stack traces for troubleshooting:

```bash
OMTRA_DEBUG=1 omtra --task denovo_ligand_condensed --n_samples 10
```

**Sources:** [readme.md:199-213](), [readme.md:512-516]()

## Web Application

OMTRA includes an interactive web interface for exploring generation tasks:

### Starting the Web Application

```bash
cd omtra_webapp
docker-compose up -d
```

Access at `http://localhost:5900` (default port). The web application provides:
- Interactive task selection
- File upload for proteins, ligands, pharmacophores
- Real-time visualization of generated structures
- Downloadable results

See `omtra_webapp/START.md` for detailed configuration options.

**Sources:** [readme.md:520-544]()

**Sources:** [readme.md:1-558]()

# Page: Installation and Setup

# Installation and Setup

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [readme.md](readme.md)

</details>



This page provides comprehensive instructions for installing OMTRA and preparing your environment for training and sampling. It covers both manual (conda/mamba) and Docker-based installation methods, model weight acquisition, and installation verification.

For information about running OMTRA commands after installation, see [Command Line Interface](#2.2). For quick examples of common usage patterns, see [Quick Start Examples](#2.3).

---

## System Requirements

OMTRA requires the following system configuration:

| Requirement | Specification |
|------------|---------------|
| Operating System | Linux (tested on Ubuntu 20.04+) |
| GPU | NVIDIA GPU with CUDA support |
| CUDA Version | 12.1 (recommended) |
| Python | 3.11 |
| RAM | 16GB+ recommended |
| Disk Space | ~10GB for dependencies, ~5GB for model weights |

**Sources:** [readme.md:47-51]()

---

## Installation Methods Overview

OMTRA offers two installation approaches:

```mermaid
graph TB
    Start["Installation Decision"]
    
    Manual["Manual Installation<br/>(conda/mamba)"]
    Docker["Docker Installation<br/>(containerized)"]
    
    ManualSteps["1. Create conda environment<br/>2. Clone repository<br/>3. Run build_env.sh<br/>4. Install via pip"]
    DockerSteps["1. Install Docker + NVIDIA toolkit<br/>2. Pull pre-built image OR<br/>3. Build from Dockerfile"]
    
    ManualResult["omtra command available<br/>in conda environment"]
    DockerResult["omtra shell function<br/>wraps Docker container"]
    
    Weights["Download Model Weights<br/>wget from bits.csb.pitt.edu"]
    
    Verify["Verify Installation<br/>omtra --help"]
    
    Start -->|"Development<br/>Direct control"| Manual
    Start -->|"Deployment<br/>Isolation"| Docker
    
    Manual --> ManualSteps
    Docker --> DockerSteps
    
    ManualSteps --> ManualResult
    DockerSteps --> DockerResult
    
    ManualResult --> Weights
    DockerResult --> Weights
    
    Weights --> Verify
```

**Comparison:**

| Aspect | Manual Installation | Docker Installation |
|--------|-------------------|-------------------|
| **Best For** | Development, debugging, training | Deployment, web app, reproducibility |
| **Setup Complexity** | Moderate (dependency management) | Low (pre-configured) |
| **Disk Space** | ~10GB (environment only) | ~15GB (includes container) |
| **GPU Access** | Direct | Via NVIDIA Container Toolkit |
| **File Access** | Direct filesystem | Volume mounts |
| **Customization** | Full control | Limited to Dockerfile/compose |

**Sources:** [readme.md:41-46](), [readme.md:53-80](), [readme.md:80-138]()

---

## Manual Installation (Recommended)

The manual installation provides direct access to the Python environment and is recommended for most users, especially those who want to develop or train models.

### Installation Flow Diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Environment Setup"
        Conda["mamba create -n omtra<br/>python=3.11"]
        Activate["mamba activate omtra"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Repository"
        Clone["git clone<br/>gnina/OMTRA"]
        CD["cd OMTRA"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Build Process"
        BuildScript["./build_env.sh"]
        
        subgraph "build_env.sh installs:"
            PyTorch["PyTorch 2.x<br/>(CUDA 12.1)"]
            DGL["DGL 2.x<br/>(CUDA 12.1)"]
            PyG["PyTorch Geometric<br/>(CUDA 12.1)"]
            OMTRA["pip install -e .<br/>(editable mode)"]
        end
    end
    
    subgraph "Result"
        CLI["omtra command<br/>available in PATH"]
    end
    
    Conda --> Activate
    Activate --> Clone
    Clone --> CD
    CD --> BuildScript
    
    BuildScript --> PyTorch
    BuildScript --> DGL
    BuildScript --> PyG
    BuildScript --> OMTRA
    
    PyTorch --> CLI
    DGL --> CLI
    PyG --> CLI
    OMTRA --> CLI
```

### Step-by-Step Instructions

**1. Create and activate conda environment:**

```bash
mamba create -n omtra python=3.11
mamba activate omtra
```

**Note:** You can use `conda` instead of `mamba`, but `mamba` is faster for dependency resolution.

**2. Clone the repository:**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/gnina/OMTRA.git
cd OMTRA
```

**3. Run the build script:**

```bash
chmod +x build_env.sh
./build_env.sh
```

The `build_env.sh` script performs the following operations:

| Step | Action | Purpose |
|------|--------|---------|
| 1 | Install PyTorch with CUDA 12.1 | Core deep learning framework |
| 2 | Install DGL with CUDA 12.1 | Graph neural network library |
| 3 | Install PyG with CUDA 12.1 | Additional graph layers |
| 4 | `pip install -e .` | Install OMTRA package in editable mode |

**4. Verify installation:**

```bash
omtra --help
```

You should see the OMTRA CLI help text. The `omtra` command is installed as an entry point defined in `setup.py`.

**Sources:** [readme.md:53-78]()

---

## Docker Installation

Docker installation provides an isolated, reproducible environment and is required for the web application. It uses the NVIDIA Container Toolkit to provide GPU access to containers.

### Docker Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Host System"
        DockerEngine["Docker Engine"]
        NVToolkit["NVIDIA Container Toolkit"]
        GPU["NVIDIA GPU"]
        
        Filesystem["Host Filesystem<br/>- OMTRA/omtra/trained_models<br/>- User output directories"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Docker Container"
        Image["gnina/omtra:latest<br/>(Docker Hub)"]
        
        subgraph "Container Environment"
            CondaEnv["Conda Environment<br/>python=3.11"]
            Installed["Installed Packages<br/>- PyTorch + CUDA<br/>- DGL + CUDA<br/>- PyG + CUDA<br/>- OMTRA package"]
            EntryPoint["/app/entrypoint.sh<br/>Launches omtra CLI"]
        end
        
        Volumes["Volume Mounts<br/>- /models (ro)<br/>- /workspace (rw)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Shell Function"
        ShellFunc["omtra() function<br/>from docker-cli-setup.sh"]
        DockerRun["docker run command<br/>--gpus all<br/>--volume mounts<br/>--workdir /workspace"]
    end
    
    User["User Command<br/>omtra --task X"]
    
    NVToolkit --> GPU
    DockerEngine --> NVToolkit
    
    Image --> CondaEnv
    CondaEnv --> Installed
    Installed --> EntryPoint
    
    Filesystem --> Volumes
    Volumes --> EntryPoint
    
    User --> ShellFunc
    ShellFunc --> DockerRun
    DockerRun --> DockerEngine
    DockerEngine --> Image
```

### Prerequisites

Before using Docker installation, ensure you have:

1. **Docker and Docker Compose** - Follow [official Docker installation guide](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/)
2. **NVIDIA Container Toolkit** - Follow [NVIDIA installation guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/cloud-native/container-toolkit/install-guide.html)
3. **Model weights** - Downloaded to `omtra/trained_models/` directory (see [Model Weights section](#model-weights))

### Using the Pre-built Image

The simplest approach is to use the pre-built image from Docker Hub:

```bash
cd OMTRA
source docker-cli-setup.sh
omtra --task denovo_ligand_condensed --n_samples 10
```

The `docker-cli-setup.sh` script creates a shell function that:

1. Pulls `gnina/omtra:latest` from Docker Hub (first run only)
2. Sets up volume mounts for model weights and output directories
3. Configures GPU access via `--gpus all`
4. Wraps all arguments and passes them to the container

### Building Locally (Optional)

To build the Docker image yourself:

```bash
cd OMTRA
docker build -t gnina/omtra:latest .
source docker-cli-setup.sh
```

The `Dockerfile` defines the container build process (not shown but referenced in readme).

### Shell Function Configuration

The `docker-cli-setup.sh` script supports customization via environment variables:

| Environment Variable | Purpose | Default |
|---------------------|---------|---------|
| `OMTRA_CLI_IMAGE` | Docker image name and tag | `gnina/omtra:latest` |
| `OMTRA_NO_GPU` | Disable GPU support (for testing) | Not set (GPU enabled) |
| `OMTRA_MODELS_DIR` | Path to model weights | `$PWD/omtra/trained_models` |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Use a specific version
export OMTRA_CLI_IMAGE="gnina/omtra:v1.0.0"
source docker-cli-setup.sh

# Disable GPU for testing
export OMTRA_NO_GPU=1
source docker-cli-setup.sh
```

### Making the CLI Available Permanently

Add to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`:

```bash
source /path/to/OMTRA/docker-cli-setup.sh
```

**Sources:** [readme.md:80-138]()

---

## Model Weights

OMTRA requires pre-trained model weights for sampling. These checkpoints are not included in the repository and must be downloaded separately.

### Download Location

```mermaid
graph LR
    Source["bits.csb.pitt.edu<br/>/files/OMTRA/omtra_v0_weights/"]
    
    Download["wget -r -np -nH<br/>--cut-dirs=3<br/>-R 'index.html*'"]
    
    Target["OMTRA/omtra/trained_models/<br/>- denovo_ligand_condensed.ckpt<br/>- fixed_protein_ligand_denovo_condensed.ckpt<br/>- rigid_docking_condensed.ckpt<br/>- ligand_conformer_condensed.ckpt<br/>- etc."]
    
    CLI["omtra command<br/>--checkpoint flag<br/>(auto-selects based on --task)"]
    
    Source --> Download
    Download --> Target
    Target --> CLI
```

### Download Command

From the `OMTRA` repository root:

```bash
wget -r -np -nH --cut-dirs=3 -R "index.html*" \
  -P omtra/trained_models \
  https://bits.csb.pitt.edu/files/OMTRA/omtra_v0_weights/
```

**Command explanation:**

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `-r` | Recursive download |
| `-np` | No parent directories |
| `-nH` | No host directory |
| `--cut-dirs=3` | Remove 3 directory levels from path |
| `-R "index.html*"` | Reject index files |
| `-P omtra/trained_models` | Save to this directory |

### Expected Directory Structure

After download, you should have:

```
OMTRA/
└── omtra/
    └── trained_models/
        ├── denovo_ligand_condensed.ckpt
        ├── fixed_protein_ligand_denovo_condensed.ckpt
        ├── rigid_docking_condensed.ckpt
        ├── ligand_conformer_condensed.ckpt
        ├── denovo_ligand_from_pharmacophore_condensed.ckpt
        ├── ligand_conformer_from_pharmacophore_condensed.ckpt
        ├── fixed_protein_pharmacophore_ligand_denovo_condensed.ckpt
        └── rigid_docking_pharmacophore_condensed.ckpt
```

### Checkpoint Selection

The `omtra` CLI automatically selects the appropriate checkpoint based on the `--task` argument. The mapping is:

| Task | Checkpoint File |
|------|----------------|
| `denovo_ligand_condensed` | `denovo_ligand_condensed.ckpt` |
| `fixed_protein_ligand_denovo_condensed` | `fixed_protein_ligand_denovo_condensed.ckpt` |
| `rigid_docking_condensed` | `rigid_docking_condensed.ckpt` |
| `ligand_conformer_condensed` | `ligand_conformer_condensed.ckpt` |
| `denovo_ligand_from_pharmacophore_condensed` | `denovo_ligand_from_pharmacophore_condensed.ckpt` |

You can override the automatic selection with `--checkpoint`:

```bash
omtra --task denovo_ligand_condensed \
  --checkpoint /path/to/custom/checkpoint.ckpt \
  --n_samples 10
```

**Sources:** [readme.md:141-149]()

## Verification

After installation, verify that OMTRA is working correctly:

### Basic Verification

```bash
# Check CLI is available
omtra --help

# Expected output: OMTRA help text with available arguments
```

### Test Sample Generation

Run a minimal sampling test:

```bash
# Manual installation
omtra --task denovo_ligand_condensed \
  --n_samples 1 \
  --output_dir test_output

# Docker installation  
# (same command - docker-cli-setup.sh handles the container)
omtra --task denovo_ligand_condensed \
  --n_samples 1 \
  --output_dir test_output
```

### Expected Results

```
├── ligands/
```

To verify evaluation metrics work:

```bash
omtra --task denovo_ligand_condensed \
```

```
test_output/
├── ligands/
│   ├── sample_0.sdf
│   ├── sample_1.sdf
│   ├── sample_2.sdf
│   ├── sample_3.sdf
│   └── sample_4.sdf
```

**Key installation components:**

|-----------|----------|---------|

| `docker-cli-setup.sh` | Repository root | Creates shell function wrapper for Docker CLI |
| `Dockerfile` | Repository root | Docker image build definition |
| `omtra/` | Package directory | Main Python package |
| `routines/sample.py` | Sampling script | Invoked by `omtra` CLI for generation |
| `routines/train.py` | Training script | Used for model training |
| `configs/` | Configuration files | Hydra configs for tasks and training |

## Troubleshooting

### Common Issues

| Issue | Cause | Solution |
|-------|-------|----------|
| `omtra: command not found` | Environment not activated or not in PATH | Activate conda environment: `mamba activate omtra` |
| `CUDA error: no kernel image` | CUDA version mismatch | Reinstall PyTorch/DGL with matching CUDA version |
| `FileNotFoundError: checkpoint` | Model weights not downloaded | Run wget command from [Model Weights section](#model-weights) |
| `Permission denied: ./build_env.sh` | Script not executable | Run `chmod +x build_env.sh` |
| Docker: `GPU not found` | NVIDIA Container Toolkit not installed | Install toolkit per NVIDIA docs |
| Docker: `Cannot connect to Docker daemon` | Docker service not running | `sudo systemctl start docker` |

### Debug Mode

Enable verbose error output:

```bash
# Set environment variable
export OMTRA_DEBUG=1

# Run command
omtra --task denovo_ligand_condensed --n_samples 1
```

This provides full stack traces for debugging issues.

### Verifying CUDA Setup

Check GPU visibility:

```python
# Manual installation
python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available()); print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))"

# Docker installation
docker run --rm --gpus all gnina/omtra:latest \
  python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())"
```

Expected output: `True` and your GPU name.

**Sources:** [readme.md:512-516]()

# Page: Command Line Interface

# Command Line Interface

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [configs/eval/default.yaml](configs/eval/default.yaml)
- [omtra/data/graph/utils.py](omtra/data/graph/utils.py)

- [routines/sample.py](routines/sample.py)

</details>



The Command Line Interface (CLI) provides the primary method for running OMTRA sampling tasks from the command line. This page documents the `omtra` command, its arguments, and subcommands.

For information about installation and setup, see [Installation and Setup](#2.1). For practical examples and common workflows, see [Quick Start Examples](#2.3). For detailed information about the underlying sampling pipeline, see [Sampling Pipeline](#8.1).

---

## Overview

The `omtra` command is the main entry point for running molecular generation tasks. It is available after installation via either manual setup or Docker. The CLI interfaces with the sampling routine implemented in [routines/sample.py](), which orchestrates model loading, data preparation, generation, and output writing.

Two primary CLI modes are available:

1. **Sampling mode**: Generate molecules using trained models (`omtra --task <task> [options]`)
2. **Utility mode**: Convert molecular structures to pharmacophore representations (`omtra mol2pharm`)

---

## CLI Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "CLI Entry Points"
        CLI["omtra command"]
        Sample["omtra --task ..."]
        Mol2Pharm["omtra mol2pharm"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Argument Parsing"
        ParseArgs["parse_args()<br/>routines/sample.py:34-158"]
        ArgGroups["Argument Groups<br/>Core, Input Files,<br/>Advanced, Metrics"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Main Execution"
        Main["main(args)<br/>routines/sample.py:273-500"]
        LoadCkpt["Load Checkpoint<br/>omtra_from_checkpoint()"]
        GetTask["Get Task Definition<br/>task_name_to_class()"]
        LoadData["Load Dataset<br/>(conditional only)"]
        SampleModel["model.sample()<br/>Generate molecules"]
        WriteOutput["Write Output Files<br/>SDF/CIF/XYZ"]
        ComputeMetrics["Compute Metrics<br/>(if --metrics flag)"]
    end
    
    CLI --> Sample
    CLI --> Mol2Pharm
    Sample --> ParseArgs
    ParseArgs --> ArgGroups
    ArgGroups --> Main
    
    Main --> LoadCkpt
    Main --> GetTask
    Main --> LoadData
    Main --> SampleModel
    SampleModel --> WriteOutput
    Main --> ComputeMetrics
    
    style Sample fill:#f9f9f9
    style Main fill:#f9f9f9
    style SampleModel fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Sources:** [readme.md:159-196](), [routines/sample.py:34-158](), [routines/sample.py:273-500]()

---

## Command Structure

### Basic Invocation

```bash
omtra --task <task_name> [options]
```

The `--task` argument is required and specifies which generation task to perform. All other arguments are optional with sensible defaults.

### Implementation Details

The CLI is implemented through the `parse_args()` function which defines all command-line arguments, and the `main()` function which orchestrates the sampling workflow:

| Component | Location | Purpose |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| Argument parser | [routines/sample.py:34-158]() | Defines all CLI arguments and their types |
| Main routine | [routines/sample.py:273-500]() | Orchestrates model loading, sampling, and output |
| Checkpoint loading | [omtra/load/quick.py]() | Loads trained model from checkpoint |
| Task registry | [omtra/tasks/register.py]() | Maps task names to Task classes |

**Sources:** [routines/sample.py:34-158](), [routines/sample.py:273-500]()

---

## Core Arguments

These arguments control the fundamental sampling behavior:

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--task` | string | *required* | Sampling task name (see [Available Tasks](#available-tasks)) |
| `--checkpoint` | path | `args.checkpoint` | Path to model checkpoint file |
| `--n_samples` | int | 100 | Number of samples to generate |
| `--n_timesteps` | int | 250 | Number of integration steps during generation |
| `--output_dir` | path | auto | Directory for output files |
| `--metrics` | flag | False | Compute evaluation metrics after generation |

### Implementation

These arguments are parsed in [routines/sample.py:38-99]():

```python
p.add_argument("checkpoint", type=Path, help="Path to the model checkpoint (required)")
p.add_argument("--task", type=str, help="Task to sample for (e.g. denovo_ligand)", required=True)
p.add_argument("--n_samples", type=int, default=100, help="Number of samples to draw")
p.add_argument("--n_timesteps", type=int, default=250, help="Number of integration steps")
p.add_argument("--output_dir", type=Path, default=None, help="Directory to write outputs to")
p.add_argument("--metrics", action="store_true", help="If set, compute metrics for the samples")
```

### Checkpoint Selection

When `--checkpoint` is not explicitly provided, the CLI automatically selects the appropriate checkpoint based on the task name. Pre-trained checkpoints are stored in `omtra/trained_models/` and loaded via `quick_load.omtra_from_checkpoint()` at [routines/sample.py:282]().

**Sources:** [readme.md:169-179](), [routines/sample.py:38-99](), [routines/sample.py:274-282]()

---

## Input File Arguments

For conditional generation tasks, these arguments specify input structures:

| Argument | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `--protein_file` | path | Protein structure (PDB or CIF format) |
| `--ligand_file` | path | Ligand structure (SDF format) |
| `--pharmacophore_file` | path | Pharmacophore constraints (JSON, XYZ, or SDF format) |

### Pocket Definition Arguments

When using `--protein_file`, one of the following methods must be used to define the binding pocket:

| Argument | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `--pocket_ligand` | path | Reference ligand SDF to define pocket center |
| `--pocket_center` | string | Pocket center as 'x,y,z' coordinates |
| `--pocket_residues` | string | Residues defining pocket (format: 'CHAIN:RESID,CHAIN:START-END') |
| `--bbox_length` | float | Bounding box size in Angstroms (default: 23.0) |

### Input Processing Flow

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Input Files"
        ProtFile["--protein_file<br/>PDB/CIF"]
        LigFile["--ligand_file<br/>SDF"]
        PharmFile["--pharmacophore_file<br/>JSON/XYZ/SDF"]
        PocketDef["Pocket Definition<br/>--pocket_ligand<br/>--pocket_center<br/>--pocket_residues"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Processing"
        LoadProt["Load Protein<br/>biotite.structure"]
        LoadLig["Load Ligand<br/>RDKit"]
        LoadPharm["Load/Extract Pharmacophore<br/>get_pharmacophores()"]
        DefPocket["Define Pocket Region<br/>Extract atoms in bbox"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Graph Construction"
        BuildGraph["build_complex_graph()<br/>Create DGL hetero graph"]
        SetFixed["Mark Fixed Modalities<br/>Based on task definition"]
        GList["g_list<br/>List of input graphs"]
    end
    
    ProtFile --> LoadProt
    LigFile --> LoadLig
    PharmFile --> LoadPharm
    PocketDef --> DefPocket
    
    LoadProt --> DefPocket
    DefPocket --> BuildGraph
    LoadLig --> BuildGraph
    LoadPharm --> BuildGraph
    
    BuildGraph --> SetFixed
    SetFixed --> GList
    
    style GList fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Sources:** [readme.md:182-194](), [routines/sample.py:293-296]()

---

## Advanced Sampling Options

These arguments provide fine-grained control over the generation process:

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--stochastic_sampling` | flag | False | Enable stochastic (vs deterministic) sampling |
| `--noise_scaler` | float | 1.0 | Scaling factor for noise in stochastic sampling |
| `--eps` | float | 0.01 | Epsilon value for numerical stability |
| `--visualize` | flag | False | Save generation trajectory for visualization |

### Ligand Size Control

Control the number of atoms in generated ligands:

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--use_gt_n_lig_atoms` | flag | False | Match ground truth ligand atom count |
| `--n_lig_atom_margin` | float | 0.075 | ±% margin around ground truth atom count |
| `--n_lig_atoms_mean` | float | None | Mean for atom count distribution |
| `--n_lig_atoms_std` | float | None | Standard deviation for atom count distribution |

### Dataset Arguments

For conditional sampling from existing datasets:

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--dataset` | string | 'pharmit' | Dataset to sample from |
| `--dataset_start_idx` | int | 0 | Starting index in dataset |
| `--n_replicates` | int | 1 | Replicates per input sample |
| `--split` | string | 'val' | Data split to use |
| `--sys_idx_file` | path | None | File with pre-selected indices |

**Sources:** [readme.md:197-214](), [routines/sample.py:118-156]()

---

## Available Tasks

The `--task` argument accepts the following task names:

### Unconditional Generation

| Task Name | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `denovo_ligand_condensed` | Generate novel drug-like molecules from scratch |

### Protein-Conditioned Generation

| Task Name | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `fixed_protein_ligand_denovo_condensed` | Design ligands for a fixed protein binding site |
| `protein_ligand_denovo_condensed` ⚠️ | Joint generation of ligand with flexible protein |
| `exp_apo_conditioned_denovo_ligand_condensed` ⚠️ | Generate from experimental apo structure |
| `pred_apo_conditioned_denovo_ligand_condensed` ⚠️ | Generate from predicted apo structure |

### Docking Tasks

| Task Name | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `rigid_docking_condensed` | Dock known ligand into fixed protein |
| `flexible_docking_condensed` ⚠️ | Dock with protein flexibility |
| `expapo_conditioned_ligand_docking_condensed` ⚠️ | Dock from experimental apo |
| `predapo_conditioned_ligand_docking_condensed` ⚠️ | Dock from predicted apo |

### Conformer Generation

| Task Name | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `ligand_conformer_condensed` | Generate 3D conformations for given ligand |

### Pharmacophore-Conditioned Tasks

| Task Name | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `denovo_ligand_pharmacophore_condensed` ⚠️ | Generate ligand and pharmacophore jointly |
| `denovo_ligand_from_pharmacophore_condensed` | Design ligand matching pharmacophore |
| `ligand_conformer_from_pharmacophore_condensed` | Generate conformer satisfying pharmacophore |
| `fixed_protein_pharmacophore_ligand_denovo_condensed` | Design ligand for protein with pharmacophore |
| `rigid_docking_pharmacophore_condensed` | Dock with pharmacophore constraints |
| `protein_ligand_pharmacophore_denovo_condensed` ⚠️ | Joint generation with pharmacophore |

⚠️ = Checkpoint not yet available

### Task Implementation

Tasks are registered in [omtra/tasks/register.py]() and retrieved via `task_name_to_class()` at [routines/sample.py:286]():

```python
task_name: str = args.task
task: Task = task_name_to_class(task_name)
```

**Sources:** [readme.md:215-256](), [routines/sample.py:285-286]()

---

## Output Organization

### Output Directory Structure

The CLI organizes outputs based on whether the task is conditional or unconditional:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Unconditional Tasks"
        U_Out["output_dir/"]
        U_SDF["denovo_ligand_condensed_lig.sdf<br/>All generated ligands"]
        U_Out --> U_SDF
    end
    
    subgraph "Conditional Tasks"
        C_Out["output_dir/"]
        Sys0["sys_0_gt/<br/>Ground truth for system 0"]
        Sys1["sys_1_gt/<br/>Ground truth for system 1"]
        
        GT_Lig["ligand.sdf<br/>Reference ligand"]
        GT_Prot["protein.cif<br/>Reference protein"]
        GT_Pharm["pharmacophore.xyz<br/>Reference pharmacophore"]
        Gen_Lig["gen_ligands.sdf<br/>All replicates"]
        
        C_Out --> Sys0
        C_Out --> Sys1
        Sys0 --> GT_Lig
        Sys0 --> GT_Prot
        Sys0 --> GT_Pharm
        Sys0 --> Gen_Lig
    end
    
    subgraph "With --visualize Flag"
        V_Out["output_dir/sys_0_gt/"]
        V_Traj["sys_0_rep_0_lig_xt.sdf<br/>Integration trajectory"]
        V_Pred["sys_0_rep_0_lig_xhat.sdf<br/>Predicted endpoints"]
        V_Out --> V_Traj
        V_Out --> V_Pred
    end
    
    style U_SDF fill:#f9f9f9
    style Gen_Lig fill:#f9f9f9
    style V_Traj fill:#f9f9f9
```

### File Writing Implementation

Output files are written in [routines/sample.py:382-481](). The logic differs based on task type and visualization flag:

1. **Unconditional, no visualization** ([routines/sample.py:382-386]()): Single SDF file with all ligands
2. **Unconditional, with visualization** ([routines/sample.py:387-391]()): Trajectory files per system
3. **Conditional, no visualization** ([routines/sample.py:392-438]()): Organized by system with ground truth
4. **Conditional, with visualization** ([routines/sample.py:440-481]()): Trajectory files per replicate

### Output File Formats

| File Type | Extension | Writer Function |
|-----------|-----------|-----------------|
| Ligands | `.sdf` | `write_mols_to_sdf()` |
| Proteins | `.cif` | `write_arrays_to_cif()` |
| Pharmacophores | `.xyz` | `pharm_to_xyz()` |

The `SampledSystem` class ([omtra/eval/system.py:38-800]()) provides methods for writing different molecular components:

- `write_ligand()` at [omtra/eval/system.py:735-751]()
- `write_protein()` at [omtra/eval/system.py:753-768]()
- `write_pharmacophore()` at [omtra/eval/system.py:783-800]()

**Sources:** [routines/sample.py:373-481](), [omtra/eval/system.py:735-800]()

## Evaluation and Metrics

### The --metrics Flag

When `--metrics` is specified, the CLI computes evaluation metrics after generation:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Metrics Computation Flow"
        Flag["--metrics flag"]
        LoadCfg["Load Evaluation Config<br/>configs/eval/default.yaml"]
        GetEvals["Get Evaluators for Task<br/>default_eval_cfg[task_name]"]
        RunEvals["Run Each Evaluator<br/>get_eval(eval_name)()"]
        Collect["Collect Metrics<br/>metrics.update()"]
        Write["Write JSON<br/>task_name_metrics.json"]
    end
    
    Flag --> LoadCfg
    LoadCfg --> GetEvals
    GetEvals --> RunEvals
    RunEvals --> Collect
    Collect --> Write
    
    style Write fill:#f9f9f9
```

### Implementation

Metrics computation occurs in [routines/sample.py:483-498]():

```python
if args.metrics:
    default_eval_cfg = OmegaConf.load(default_eval_path)
    metrics = {}
    for eval_entry in default_eval_cfg[task_name]:
        for eval_name, config in eval_entry.items():
            metrics.update(get_eval(eval_name)(sampled_systems, config.get("params", {})))
    
    metrics_file = output_dir / f"{task_name}_metrics.json"
    with open(metrics_file, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(metrics, f)
```

### Available Metrics by Task

Metrics are configured per task in [configs/eval/default.yaml](). Common metrics include:

| Metric Category | Evaluator Function | Location |
|----------------|-------------------|----------|
| Validity | `validity()` | [omtra/eval/evals.py:37-41]() |
| Stability | `stability()` | [omtra/eval/evals.py:44-48]() |
| REOS filters | `check_reos_and_rings()` | [omtra/eval/evals.py:51-55]() |
| Geometry | `geometry()` | [omtra/eval/evals.py:58-95]() |
| Flatness | `flatness()` | [omtra/eval/evals.py:98-123]() |
| Intermolecular distance | `intermolecular_distance()` | [omtra/eval/evals.py:126-148]() |
| Ligand RMSD | `ligand_rmsd()` | [omtra/eval/evals.py:151-177]() |
| Volume overlap | `volume_overlap()` | [omtra/eval/evals.py:180-199]() |
| PoseBusters | `pb_valid_*()` | [omtra/eval/evals.py:202-322]() |
| Pharmacophore match | `check_pharm_match()` | [omtra/eval/evals.py:325-329]() |

### Metric Registration

Evaluators are registered via the `@register_eval()` decorator and retrieved through `get_eval()` from [omtra/eval/register.py]().

**Sources:** [routines/sample.py:483-498](), [omtra/eval/evals.py:1-329](), [configs/eval/default.yaml:1-684]()

## Utility Commands

### mol2pharm: Pharmacophore Extraction

The `omtra mol2pharm` command extracts pharmacophore features from ligand SDF files and outputs them in JSON format compatible with Pharmit.

#### Basic Usage

```bash
omtra mol2pharm ligand.sdf -o pharmacophore.json --pretty
```

#### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `input.sdf` | Input ligand file in SDF format |
| `-o`, `--output` | Output JSON file path |
| `--pretty` | Format JSON with indentation |
| `--verbose` | Print extracted features to console |
| `--all-disabled` | Set all features as disabled by default |
| `--first-only` | Process only first molecule in multi-molecule SDF |

#### Output Format

The tool generates JSON in Pharmit format:

```json
{
  "points": [
    {
      "name": "Aromatic",
      "x": 10.5,
      "y": 20.3,
      "z": 15.2,
      "enabled": true
    },
    {
      "name": "HydrogenAcceptor",
      "x": 8.2,
      "y": 18.7,
      "z": 14.1,
      "enabled": true
    }
  ]
}
```

#### Supported Feature Types

| Feature Type | Description |
|--------------|-------------|
| `Aromatic` | Aromatic ring centers |
| `HydrogenDonor` | H-bond donor groups |
| `HydrogenAcceptor` | H-bond acceptor atoms |
| `PositiveIon` | Positively charged groups |
| `NegativeIon` | Negatively charged groups |
| `Hydrophobic` | Hydrophobic regions |
| `Halogen` | Halogen bond donors |

Pharmacophore extraction is implemented via `get_pharmacophores()` from [omtra/data/pharmacophores.py]().

**Sources:** [readme.md:336-481]()

---

```bash
OMTRA_DEBUG=1 omtra --task denovo_ligand_condensed --n_samples 10
```

# Quick Start Examples

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [configs/eval/default.yaml](configs/eval/default.yaml)
- [omtra/data/graph/utils.py](omtra/data/graph/utils.py)

</details>



This page provides practical, copy-paste-ready examples for common OMTRA use cases. Each example includes the complete command, expected outputs, and explanation of key parameters.

**Purpose and Scope:** This guide demonstrates typical workflows for generating molecules with OMTRA's command-line interface. For complete CLI reference and all available arguments, see [Command Line Interface](#2.2). For installation instructions, see [Installation and Setup](#2.1). For understanding the underlying task system, see [Tasks and Modalities](#3.1).

---

## Prerequisites

Before running these examples:

1. **Installation completed** - Either manual or Docker installation (see [Installation and Setup](#2.1))
2. **Model weights downloaded** - Located in `omtra/trained_models/` directory
3. **GPU available** - CUDA-enabled GPU recommended for reasonable performance

Verify your installation:
```bash
omtra --help
```

---

## Quick Reference: Task Overview

The following table summarizes the available tasks with pre-trained checkpoints:

| Task | Input Requirements | Generates | Typical Use Case |
|------|-------------------|-----------|------------------|
| `denovo_ligand_condensed` | None | Ligand only | Exploring chemical space |
| `fixed_protein_ligand_denovo_condensed` | Protein PDB/CIF + pocket definition | Ligand in binding site | Structure-based drug design |
| `rigid_docking_condensed` | Protein PDB/CIF + ligand SDF | Ligand pose | Binding pose prediction |
| `ligand_conformer_condensed` | Ligand SDF | Ligand conformations | Conformer generation |
| `denovo_ligand_from_pharmacophore_condensed` | Pharmacophore JSON/XYZ/SDF | Ligand matching pharmacophore | Pharmacophore-constrained design |
| `ligand_conformer_from_pharmacophore_condensed` | Ligand SDF + pharmacophore | Conformations matching pharmacophore | Constrained conformer sampling |
| `fixed_protein_pharmacophore_ligand_denovo_condensed` | Protein + pharmacophore + pocket | Ligand in pocket with constraints | Multi-constraint SBDD |
| `rigid_docking_pharmacophore_condensed` | Protein + ligand + pharmacophore | Pose matching pharmacophore | Constrained docking |

**Sources:** [readme.md:216-256]()

---

## Example 1: Unconditional Ligand Generation

**Goal:** Generate novel drug-like molecules from scratch without constraints.

### Basic Command

```bash
omtra --task denovo_ligand_condensed \
  --n_samples 100 \
  --output_dir outputs/denovo_samples
```

### With Metrics

```bash
omtra --task denovo_ligand_condensed \
  --n_samples 100 \
  --output_dir outputs/denovo_samples \
  --metrics
```

### Output Structure

```
outputs/denovo_samples/
├── denovo_ligand_condensed_lig.sdf      # All generated molecules
└── denovo_ligand_condensed_metrics.json  # Metrics (if --metrics flag used)
```

### Understanding the Output

The SDF file contains all generated molecules as multi-structure SDF. Each molecule is a complete 3D structure with atom types, charges, and bond orders.

**Metrics computed** (when `--metrics` flag is used):
- **Validity metrics**: Fraction of chemically valid molecules
- **Stability metrics**: Fraction of atoms with valid valencies
- **REOS filters**: Drug-likeness rule violations
- **Ring system checks**: Detection of unusual/out-of-distribution ring systems
- **PoseBusters checks**: Geometry and structural quality

### Workflow Diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
    Command["omtra --task denovo_ligand_condensed"]
    Checkpoint["Auto-select checkpoint<br/>omtra/trained_models/"]
    Model["OMTRA.sample()<br/>omtra/models/omtra.py"]
    Prior["sample_priors()<br/>Gaussian noise<br/>omtra/priors/"]
    VectorField["VectorField.integrate()<br/>250 timesteps<br/>omtra/models/vector_field.py"]
    System["SampledSystem objects<br/>omtra/eval/system.py"]
    SDF["denovo_ligand_condensed_lig.sdf"]
    
    Command --> Checkpoint
    Checkpoint --> Model
    Model --> Prior
    Prior --> VectorField
    VectorField --> System
    System --> SDF
```

**Sources:** [readme.md:259-265](), [routines/sample.py:273-503]()

---

## Example 2: Structure-Based Drug Design

**Goal:** Design ligands that bind to a specific protein pocket.

### Option A: Define Pocket with Reference Ligand

```bash
omtra --task fixed_protein_ligand_denovo_condensed \
  --protein_file my_protein.pdb \
  --pocket_ligand reference_ligand.sdf \
  --n_samples 50 \
  --output_dir outputs/sbdd_samples
```

This extracts the binding pocket based on atoms within a distance threshold of the reference ligand.

### Option B: Define Pocket by Center Coordinates

```bash
omtra --task fixed_protein_ligand_denovo_condensed \
  --protein_file my_protein.pdb \
  --pocket_center 10.5,20.3,15.2 \
  --bbox_length 25.0 \
  --n_samples 50 \
  --output_dir outputs/sbdd_samples
```

**Parameters:**
- `--pocket_center`: x,y,z coordinates in Angstroms
- `--bbox_length`: Side length of cubic bounding box (default: 23.0 Å)

### Option C: Define Pocket by Residues

```bash
omtra --task fixed_protein_ligand_denovo_condensed \
  --protein_file my_protein.pdb \
  --pocket_residues A:123-130,A:200,B:50-55 \
  --n_samples 50 \
  --output_dir outputs/sbdd_samples
```

**Residue format:** `CHAIN:RESID` or `CHAIN:START-END`

### Output Structure

```
outputs/sbdd_samples/
└── sys_0_gt/
    ├── protein.cif                # Input protein structure
    └── gen_ligands.sdf           # All 50 generated ligands
```

### SBDD Workflow Diagram

```mermaid
graph TB
    Input["Input Files<br/>--protein_file<br/>--pocket_ligand or --pocket_center"]
    Parse["CLI Wrapper<br/>omtra_cli/main.py"]
    Graph["build_complex_graph()<br/>omtra/data/graph/"]
    PocketExtract["extract_pocket()<br/>Identify pocket residues"]
    GraphBuild["DGL HeteroGraph<br/>prot_atom, lig nodes<br/>lig_to_prot edges"]
    Sample["OMTRA.sample()<br/>Fixed protein condition<br/>Generate ligand"]
    Output["sys_0_gt/gen_ligands.sdf"]
    
    Input --> Parse
    Parse --> PocketExtract
    PocketExtract --> GraphBuild
    GraphBuild --> Graph
    Graph --> Sample
    Sample --> Output
```

**Sources:** [readme.md:268-295](), [routines/sample.py:348-355]()

---

## Example 3: Molecular Docking

**Goal:** Predict binding poses for a known ligand in a protein structure.

### Basic Docking Command

```bash
omtra --task rigid_docking_condensed \
  --protein_file protein.pdb \
  --ligand_file ligand.sdf \
  --n_samples 10 \
  --output_dir outputs/docking
```

### With Metrics

```bash
omtra --task rigid_docking_condensed \
  --protein_file protein.pdb \
  --ligand_file ligand.sdf \
  --n_samples 10 \
  --output_dir outputs/docking \
  --metrics
```

### Output Structure

```
outputs/docking/
└── sys_0_gt/
    ├── ligand.sdf              # Ground truth ligand
    ├── protein.cif             # Input protein
    └── gen_ligands.sdf         # 10 predicted poses
```

### Key Docking Metrics

When `--metrics` is used, the system computes:
- **RMSD**: Root-mean-square deviation from ground truth
- **Kabsch RMSD**: RMSD after optimal alignment
- **Centroid distance**: Distance between centroids
- **Volume overlap**: Protein-ligand volume overlap
- **Intermolecular distance**: Minimum distance to protein

### Docking Task Flow

```mermaid
graph LR
    Inputs["protein.pdb<br/>ligand.sdf"]
    GraphConstr["Graph Construction<br/>Both protein and ligand<br/>as fixed conditions"]
    Prior["Prior: Ligand structure<br/>Gaussian noise<br/>Identity preserved"]
    Integration["VectorField.integrate()<br/>Predict ligand pose"]
    Poses["10 predicted poses"]
    Metrics["RMSD, volume_overlap<br/>intermolecular_distance"]
    
    Inputs --> GraphConstr
    GraphConstr --> Prior
    Prior --> Integration
    Integration --> Poses
    Poses --> Metrics
```

**Sources:** [readme.md:297-304](), [configs/eval/default.yaml:180-206]()

---

## Example 4: Conformer Generation

**Goal:** Generate diverse 3D conformations for a given molecule.

### Basic Conformer Generation

```bash
omtra --task ligand_conformer_condensed \
  --ligand_file molecule.sdf \
  --n_samples 20 \
  --output_dir outputs/conformers
```

### With Evaluation

```bash
omtra --task ligand_conformer_condensed \
  --ligand_file molecule.sdf \
  --n_samples 20 \
  --output_dir outputs/conformers \
  --metrics
```

### Output Structure

```
outputs/conformers/
└── sys_0_gt/
    ├── ligand.sdf              # Input ligand (reference conformation)
    └── gen_ligands.sdf         # 20 generated conformations
```

### Conformer Metrics

Computed when `--metrics` flag is used:
- **Stability**: Valency checks
- **RMSD**: Deviation from reference conformation
- **Kabsch RMSD**: Alignment-corrected RMSD
- **Flatness**: Ring planarity checks
- **PoseBusters conformer checks**: Geometry validation

**Sources:** [readme.md:306-312](), [configs/eval/default.yaml:115-133]()

---

## Example 5: Pharmacophore-Guided Design

**Goal:** Generate molecules that satisfy specific pharmacophore constraints.

### From Pharmacophore JSON File

```bash
omtra --task denovo_ligand_from_pharmacophore_condensed \
  --pharmacophore_file constraints.json \
  --n_samples 100 \
  --output_dir outputs/pharm_guided
```

### From Reference Ligand (Auto-Extract Pharmacophore)

```bash
omtra --task denovo_ligand_from_pharmacophore_condensed \
  --pharmacophore_file reference_ligand.sdf \
  --n_samples 100 \
  --output_dir outputs/pharm_guided
```

When an SDF file is provided, OMTRA automatically extracts pharmacophore features using pattern matching (see [Pharmacophore Extraction](#6.4)).

### Creating Pharmacophore JSON

Use the built-in converter:

```bash
omtra mol2pharm ligand.sdf -o pharmacophore.json --pretty --verbose
```

**Output example:**
```json
{
  "points": [
    {
      "name": "Aromatic",
      "x": 12.456,
      "y": 8.234,
      "z": 15.789,
      "enabled": true
    },
    {
      "name": "HydrogenDonor",
      "x": 10.123,
      "y": 11.456,
      "z": 14.234,
      "enabled": true
    }
  ]
}
```

### Multi-Constraint Example: Protein + Pharmacophore

```bash
omtra --task fixed_protein_pharmacophore_ligand_denovo_condensed \
  --protein_file protein.pdb \
  --pocket_center 10.0,15.0,20.0 \
  --pharmacophore_file constraints.json \
  --n_samples 50 \
  --output_dir outputs/multi_constraint
```

### Pharmacophore Feature Types

| Feature | Description | Example Groups |
|---------|-------------|----------------|
| `Aromatic` | Aromatic ring centers | Phenyl, pyridine |
| `HydrogenDonor` | H-bond donor | NH, OH |
| `HydrogenAcceptor` | H-bond acceptor | C=O, N |
| `PositiveIon` | Positive charge | Ammonium |
| `NegativeIon` | Negative charge | Carboxylate |
| `Hydrophobic` | Lipophilic region | Alkyl chains |
| `Halogen` | Halogen bond donor | Cl, Br, F, I |

**Sources:** [readme.md:314-331](), [readme.md:333-481]()

---

## Understanding Output Files

### Output Directory Structure

The output structure depends on whether the task is unconditional or conditional:

#### Unconditional Tasks

```
outputs/denovo_samples/
├── denovo_ligand_condensed_lig.sdf       # All samples in one file
└── denovo_ligand_condensed_metrics.json   # Metrics (optional)
```

#### Conditional Tasks

```
outputs/sbdd_samples/
└── sys_0_gt/
    ├── ligand.sdf              # Ground truth ligand (if available)
    ├── protein.cif             # Input protein
    ├── pharmacophore.xyz       # Input pharmacophore (if applicable)
    └── gen_ligands.sdf         # Generated samples
```

For multiple input systems, directory pattern repeats:
```
outputs/batch_samples/
├── sys_0_gt/
│   ├── protein.cif
│   └── gen_ligands.sdf
├── sys_1_gt/
│   ├── protein.cif
│   └── gen_ligands.sdf
└── sys_2_gt/
    ├── protein.cif
    └── gen_ligands.sdf
```

### File Formats

| Extension | Format | Contains | Written By |
|-----------|--------|----------|------------|
| `.sdf` | Structure Data File | Ligand structures with 3D coords, bonds, charges | `write_mols_to_sdf()` |
| `.cif` | Crystallographic Information File | Protein structures | `write_arrays_to_cif()` |
| `.pdb` | Protein Data Bank | Protein structures (alternative) | `write_arrays_to_pdb()` |
| `.xyz` | XYZ coordinate file | Pharmacophore features | `pharm_to_xyz()` |
| `.json` | JSON | Metrics or pharmacophore definitions | `json.dump()` |

### Reading Outputs Programmatically

```python
from rdkit import Chem
import json

# Read generated ligands
supplier = Chem.SDMolSupplier('outputs/sbdd_samples/sys_0_gt/gen_ligands.sdf')
mols = [mol for mol in supplier if mol is not None]

# Read metrics
with open('outputs/denovo_samples/denovo_ligand_condensed_metrics.json') as f:
    metrics = json.load(f)
    print(f"Validity: {metrics['frac_valid_mols']:.2%}")
```

**Sources:** [omtra/eval/system.py:735-799](), [routines/sample.py:382-439]()

---

## Computing and Understanding Metrics

### Enabling Metrics

Add the `--metrics` flag to any sampling command:

```bash
omtra --task rigid_docking_condensed \
  --protein_file protein.pdb \
  --ligand_file ligand.sdf \
  --n_samples 10 \
  --output_dir outputs/docking \
  --metrics
```

### Metrics Computation Flow

```mermaid
graph TB
    Sample["Sampling Complete<br/>List of SampledSystem objects"]
    CheckFlag{"--metrics<br/>flag?"}
    LoadConfig["Load configs/eval/default.yaml"]
    GetEvals["get_eval() for each metric<br/>omtra/eval/register.py"]
    Compute["Compute metrics<br/>omtra/eval/evals.py"]
    Save["Save to JSON<br/>task_name_metrics.json"]
    
    Sample --> CheckFlag
    CheckFlag -->|Yes| LoadConfig
    CheckFlag -->|No| End["Skip metrics"]
    LoadConfig --> GetEvals
    GetEvals --> Compute
    Compute --> Save
```

### Metric Categories

The evaluation configuration is task-specific and defined in [configs/eval/default.yaml:1-684]().

#### Chemistry Validity Metrics

Computed by `validity()` evaluation function:
- **`frac_valid_mols`**: Fraction of molecules that pass RDKit sanitization
- **`avg_frag_frac`**: Average fraction of atoms in largest connected component
- **`avg_num_components`**: Average number of disconnected fragments
- **`frac_connected`**: Fraction of fully connected molecules

#### Stability Metrics

Computed by `stability()` evaluation function:
- **`frac_atoms_stable`**: Fraction of atoms with valid valencies
- **`frac_mols_stable_valence`**: Fraction of molecules with all atoms stable

#### Geometry Metrics

Computed by `geometry()` evaluation function:
- **`geometry_frac_valid_bonds`**: Fraction of bonds with physically reasonable lengths
- **`geometry_frac_valid_angles`**: Fraction of angles within acceptable ranges
- **`geometry_number_clashes`**: Average number of atomic clashes per molecule

#### RMSD Metrics (Docking/Conformer Tasks)

Computed by `ligand_rmsd()` evaluation function:
- **`ligand_rmsd`**: Standard RMSD from reference
- **`ligand_kabsch_rmsd`**: RMSD after optimal superposition
- **`ligand_centroid_distance`**: Distance between centroids

#### Protein-Ligand Interface Metrics

Computed by `intermolecular_distance()` and `volume_overlap()`:
- **`intermolecular_distance_smallest`**: Minimum distance between ligand and protein atoms
- **`volume_overlap`**: Volume overlap between ligand and protein

#### Pharmacophore Match Metrics

Computed by `pharm_match()` evaluation function:
- **`pharm_match_rate`**: Fraction of pharmacophore features satisfied
- **`pharm_match_threshold`**: Binary pass/fail based on distance threshold (default: 1.0 Å)

### Example Metrics Output

```json
{
  "frac_valid_mols": 0.92,
  "frac_atoms_stable": 0.95,
  "geometry_frac_valid_bonds": 0.98,
  "ligand_rmsd": 1.45,
  "ligand_kabsch_rmsd": 1.23,
  "intermolecular_distance_smallest": 2.1,
  "volume_overlap": 0.05,
  "pb_valid_unconditional": 0.88
}
```

**Sources:** [routines/sample.py:483-498](), [omtra/eval/evals.py:1-329](), [configs/eval/default.yaml:1-684]()

---

## Common Patterns and Advanced Options

### Controlling Ligand Size

#### Use Ground Truth Size (with margin)

```bash
omtra --task fixed_protein_ligand_denovo_condensed \
  --protein_file protein.pdb \
  --pocket_ligand reference.sdf \
  --use_gt_n_lig_atoms \
  --n_lig_atom_margin 0.15 \
  --n_samples 50 \
  --output_dir outputs/size_controlled
```

- `--use_gt_n_lig_atoms`: Match reference ligand atom count
- `--n_lig_atom_margin`: Allow ±15% variation (default: 0.075)

#### Specify Size Distribution

```bash
omtra --task fixed_protein_ligand_denovo_condensed \
  --protein_file protein.pdb \
  --pocket_center 10.0,15.0,20.0 \
  --n_lig_atoms_mean 25 \
  --n_lig_atoms_std 5 \
  --n_samples 50 \
  --output_dir outputs/custom_size
```

### Stochastic vs Deterministic Sampling

#### Deterministic (Default)

```bash
omtra --task denovo_ligand_condensed --n_samples 10
```

#### Stochastic (More Diverse)

```bash
omtra --task denovo_ligand_condensed \
  --n_samples 10 \
  --stochastic_sampling \
  --noise_scaler 1.0 \
  --eps 0.01
```

**Parameters:**
- `--stochastic_sampling`: Enable noise injection during integration
- `--noise_scaler`: Scale factor for noise (higher = more diversity)
- `--eps`: Small epsilon for numerical stability

### Adjusting Integration Steps

More steps = higher quality but slower:

```bash
omtra --task rigid_docking_condensed \
  --protein_file protein.pdb \
  --ligand_file ligand.sdf \
  --n_timesteps 500 \
  --n_samples 10
```

**Default:** 250 timesteps  
**Typical range:** 100-500 timesteps

### Batch Processing Multiple Inputs

For processing many protein-ligand pairs, save system indices to a file:

```bash
# Create index file
echo "0,5,10,15,20" > system_indices.txt

# Sample from specific systems
omtra --task rigid_docking_condensed \
  --dataset plinder \
  --sys_idx_file system_indices.txt \
  --n_replicates 5 \
  --output_dir outputs/batch
```

This generates 5 replicates for each of 5 systems (25 total samples).

### Visualizing Sampling Trajectories

Generate intermediate structures during generation:

```bash
omtra --task denovo_ligand_condensed \
  --n_samples 5 \
  --visualize \
  --output_dir outputs/trajectory
```

**Output:**
```
outputs/trajectory/
├── sys0_xt.sdf        # Noisy trajectory (x_t values)
└── sys0_xhat.sdf      # Predicted trajectory (denoised predictions)
```

Each SDF contains multiple conformations showing the generation process from noise to final structure.

### Debug Mode

For troubleshooting, enable full stack traces:

```bash
OMTRA_DEBUG=1 omtra --task denovo_ligand_condensed --n_samples 10
```

**Sources:** [routines/sample.py:34-157](), [readme.md:512-517]()

---

## Task Selection Guide

Use this decision tree to choose the appropriate task:

```mermaid
graph TD
    Start["What do you want to generate?"]
    
    Start --> Uncond{"Starting from<br/>scratch?"}
    Uncond -->|Yes| UnCondLig["denovo_ligand_condensed"]
    Uncond -->|No| HasProt{"Have protein<br/>structure?"}
    
    HasProt -->|No| HasLig{"Have ligand<br/>structure?"}
    HasProt -->|Yes| ProtFixed{"Protein<br/>fixed?"}
    
    ProtFixed -->|Yes| HasPharm1{"Pharmacophore<br/>constraints?"}
    ProtFixed -->|No| HasPharm2{"Pharmacophore<br/>constraints?"}
    
    HasPharm1 -->|Yes| FixedProtPharm["fixed_protein_pharmacophore_<br/>ligand_denovo_condensed"]
    HasPharm1 -->|No| FixedProt["fixed_protein_ligand_<br/>denovo_condensed"]
    
    HasPharm2 -->|Yes| FlexProtPharm["protein_ligand_<br/>pharmacophore_denovo_condensed"]
    HasPharm2 -->|No| FlexProt["protein_ligand_<br/>denovo_condensed"]
    
    HasLig -->|Yes| LigConf{"Generate<br/>conformers?"}
    HasLig -->|No| JustPharm["denovo_ligand_from_<br/>pharmacophore_condensed"]
    
    LigConf -->|Yes| ConfPharm{"Pharmacophore<br/>constraints?"}
    LigConf -->|No| ProtLigDock{"Dock into<br/>protein?"}
    
    ConfPharm -->|Yes| ConfPharmTask["ligand_conformer_from_<br/>pharmacophore_condensed"]
    ConfPharm -->|No| ConfTask["ligand_conformer_<br/>condensed"]
    
    ProtLigDock -->|Yes| DockPharm{"Pharmacophore<br/>constraints?"}
    ProtLigDock -->|No| ConfTask2["ligand_conformer_<br/>condensed"]
    
    DockPharm -->|Yes| DockPharmTask["rigid_docking_<br/>pharmacophore_condensed"]
    DockPharm -->|No| DockTask["rigid_docking_<br/>condensed"]
```

**Sources:** [readme.md:216-256](), [omtra/tasks/register.py]()

# Core Concepts

<details>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [omtra/models/self_conditioning.py](omtra/models/self_conditioning.py)
