This page provides a comprehensive guide to training OMTRA models. It covers the training pipeline architecture, data flow, key components, and the mechanics of multi-task learning. For detailed information on specific aspects, see:
- Configuration details: [Configuration System](#7.2)
- Multi-task sampling and balancing: [Multi-Task Learning](#7.3)  
- Loss function specifics: [Loss Functions and Objectives](#7.4)

For information about the datasets used during training, see [Datasets and Data Loading](#5).

## Starting Training

Training is initiated through the `omtra` CLI or directly via the training script:

```bash
# Using the CLI
omtra train \
    --config-name config \
    name=my_training_run \
    max_steps=100000 \
    edges_per_batch=300000

# Or directly
python routines/train.py \
    name=my_training_run \
    max_steps=100000
```

The training script [routines/train.py:55-191]() orchestrates the entire training process:

1. Loads configuration via Hydra
2. Initializes the data module
3. Loads or creates the model
4. Configures logging (WandB)
5. Sets up PyTorch Lightning trainer
6. Runs training loop

**Sources:** [routines/train.py:55-191]()

## Training Pipeline Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Entry Point"
        CLI["omtra train command<br/>routines/train.py:main"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Configuration"
        Hydra["Hydra Config System<br/>configs/config.yaml"]
        TaskPhases["task_phases<br/>Phase boundaries & probs"]
        TDCoupling["TaskDatasetCoupling<br/>Task-dataset mappings"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Components"
        DataModule["MultiTaskDataModule<br/>omtra/dataset/data_module.py"]
        MultiDataset["MultitaskDataSet<br/>omtra/dataset/multitask.py"]
        Sampler["MultiTaskSampler<br/>omtra/dataset/samplers.py"]
        ChunkTracker["GraphChunkTracker<br/>omtra/dataset/chunk_tracker.py"]
        
        DataModule --> MultiDataset
        DataModule --> Sampler
        Sampler --> ChunkTracker
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Components"
        OMTRA["OMTRA<br/>pl.LightningModule<br/>omtra/models/omtra.py"]
        VF["VectorField<br/>omtra/models/vector_field.py"]
        SC["SelfConditioningResidualLayer<br/>omtra/models/self_conditioning.py"]
        
        OMTRA --> VF
        OMTRA --> SC
    end
    
    subgraph "Training Loop"
        Trainer["pl.Trainer<br/>PyTorch Lightning"]
        TrainStep["training_step<br/>omtra/models/omtra.py:269"]
        Forward["forward<br/>omtra/models/omtra.py:386"]
        LossFn["Loss Computation<br/>Flow matching + Aux"]
    end
    
    CLI --> Hydra
    Hydra --> TaskPhases
    Hydra --> TDCoupling
    Hydra --> DataModule
    Hydra --> OMTRA
    
    DataModule --> Trainer
    OMTRA --> Trainer
    
    Trainer --> TrainStep
    TrainStep --> Forward
    Forward --> VF
    Forward --> LossFn
```

**Sources:** [routines/train.py:55-191](), [omtra/models/omtra.py:55-186](), [omtra/dataset/data_module.py:15-143]()

## Training Step Workflow

Each training iteration follows this sequence:

```mermaid
graph TB
    Start["training_step called<br/>batch_data = g, task_name, dataset_name"]
    
    Checkpoint["Check if checkpoint needed<br/>manual_checkpoint"]
    
    CountSamples["Count total batch size<br/>across all devices<br/>Log sample counts"]
    
    Forward["forward<br/>Compute losses"]
    
    subgraph "Forward Pass Detail"
        SampleTime["Sample time t ~ U(0,1)<br/>or Beta distribution"]
        GetBatch["Get batch indices<br/>get_batch_idxs"]
        CondPath["Sample conditional path<br/>sample_conditional_path<br/>Interpolate x_0 to x_1"]
        VFForward["VectorField.forward<br/>Predict destinations"]
        ComputeLoss["Compute losses<br/>Flow matching + Auxiliary"]
    end
    
    Aggregate["Aggregate losses<br/>Log to WandB"]
    
    Backward["Backward pass<br/>handled by Trainer"]
    
    Start --> Checkpoint
    Checkpoint --> CountSamples
    CountSamples --> Forward
    
    Forward --> SampleTime
    SampleTime --> GetBatch
    GetBatch --> CondPath
    CondPath --> VFForward
    VFForward --> ComputeLoss
    
    ComputeLoss --> Aggregate
    Aggregate --> Backward
```

**Key methods:**

| Method | Location | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| `training_step` | [omtra/models/omtra.py:269-322]() | Main training step, called by PyTorch Lightning |
| `forward` | [omtra/models/omtra.py:386-516]() | Samples time, applies conditional path, computes losses |
| `sample_conditional_path` | [omtra/models/omtra.py:542-600]() | Interpolates between x_0 and x_1 at time t |
| `manual_checkpoint` | [omtra/models/omtra.py:201-224]() | Saves checkpoints at intervals |

**Sources:** [omtra/models/omtra.py:269-516]()

## Data Flow Through Training

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Batch Construction"
        Phase["Determine current phase<br/>based on batch_idx"]
        SampleTD["Sample task & dataset<br/>according to p_dataset_task"]
        ChunkSelect["Select graph chunk<br/>ChunkTracker"]
        LoadGraphs["Load graphs from Zarr<br/>adaptive_batch_loader"]
        Batch["Batch into DGL graph<br/>dgl.batch"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Processing"
        PriorSample["Sample x_0 from priors<br/>for generated modalities"]
        TimeInterp["Interpolate to x_t<br/>x_t = α_t·x_0 + β_t·x_1"]
        BuildEdges["Build task-specific edges<br/>build_edges"]
        GNN["VectorField GNN<br/>Predict destinations"]
        Loss["Compute losses<br/>Compare predictions to x_1"]
    end
    
    Phase --> SampleTD
    SampleTD --> ChunkSelect
    ChunkSelect --> LoadGraphs
    LoadGraphs --> Batch
    
    Batch --> PriorSample
    PriorSample --> TimeInterp
    TimeInterp --> BuildEdges
    BuildEdges --> GNN
    GNN --> Loss
```

### Batch Construction Details

The `MultiTaskSampler` [omtra/dataset/samplers.py:14-180]() constructs batches:

1. **Phase determination**: Current batch index determines which phase (and thus which task-dataset probabilities) to use
2. **Task-dataset sampling**: Sample (task, dataset) pair according to `p_dataset_task[phase_idx]`
3. **Chunk selection**: `GraphChunkTracker` manages chunks from the Zarr store
4. **Adaptive loading**: `adaptive_batch_loader` [omtra/dataset/chunk_tracker.py:72-144]() selects graphs until `edges_per_batch` limit is reached
5. **Batching**: Graphs are batched using `dgl.batch` in the collate function

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/samplers.py:14-180](), [omtra/dataset/chunk_tracker.py:8-145]()

## Key Training Components

### OMTRA Model Class

The `OMTRA` class [omtra/models/omtra.py:55-1002]() is a PyTorch Lightning module that encapsulates:

| Component | Attribute | Purpose |
|-----------|-----------|---------|
| Task-dataset coupling | `td_coupling` | Defines valid task-dataset pairs and probabilities |
| Vector field | `vector_field` | GNN that predicts trajectory destinations |
| Interpolant scheduler | `interpolant_scheduler` | Computes α_t and β_t for conditional paths |
| Loss functions | `loss_fn_dict` | MSE for continuous, CrossEntropy for categorical |
| Auxiliary losses | `aux_loss_fn_dict` | Additional regularization losses |
| Optimizer config | `optimizer_cfg` | Adam optimizer configuration |

**Initialization parameters:**

```python
OMTRA(
    task_phases: DictConfig,              # Phase definitions
    task_dataset_coupling: DictConfig,    # Task-dataset mappings
    dists_file: str,                      # Path to distribution files
    graph_config: DictConfig,             # Graph construction config
    conditional_paths: DictConfig,        # Conditional path functions
    optimizer: DictConfig,                # Optimizer settings
    vector_field: DictConfig,             # VectorField architecture
    aux_losses: DictConfig,               # Auxiliary loss configs
    prior_config: DictConfig,             # Prior configurations
    time_scaled_loss: bool = False,       # Enable time-weighted losses
    train_t_dist: str = 'uniform',        # Time sampling distribution
    ...
)
```

**Sources:** [omtra/models/omtra.py:55-186]()

### MultiTaskDataModule

The `MultiTaskDataModule` [omtra/dataset/data_module.py:15-143]() manages all data loading:

```python
MultiTaskDataModule(
    dataset_config: DictConfig,           # Per-dataset configurations
    task_phases: DictConfig,              # Phase boundaries
    dataset_task_coupling: DictConfig,    # Task-dataset probs
    graph_config: DictConfig,             # Graph construction
    prior_config: DictConfig,             # Prior sampling
    edges_per_batch: int,                 # Batch size constraint
    num_workers: int = 0,                 # DataLoader workers
    max_steps: int = None,                # Training duration
    fake_atom_p: float = 0.0,            # Fake atom probability
)
```

**Responsibilities:**
- Creates separate train and validation datasets
- Instantiates `MultiTaskSampler` for each split
- Configures DataLoaders with appropriate workers and batching

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/data_module.py:15-143]()

### VectorField GNN

The `VectorField` [omtra/models/vector_field.py:40-831]() performs the core denoising:

| Component | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| Token embeddings | Embed categorical features (atom types, charges, bond orders) |
| Scalar embedding | Initial node feature embedding |
| Edge embedding | Initial edge feature embedding |
| Conv layers | `HeteroGVPConv` layers for message passing |
| Node position updaters | `NodePositionUpdate` modules for coordinate refinement |
| Edge updaters | `EdgeUpdate` modules for edge feature refinement |
| Output heads | Predict final states for each modality |

**Forward pass sequence:**
1. Embed input features (categorical → tokens, continuous → scalars)
2. Build task-specific edges
3. Apply self-conditioning (if enabled)
4. Iterate through GNN layers with interleaved position updates
5. Apply output heads to generate predictions

**Sources:** [omtra/models/vector_field.py:40-731]()

## Time Sampling and Conditional Paths

Training samples time points and interpolates between x_0 (prior) and x_1 (target):

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Time Sampling"
        SampleT["Sample t ~ U(0,1)<br/>or t ~ Beta(α,1)"]
        ComputeWeights["Compute α_t, β_t<br/>InterpolantScheduler"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Conditional Path Sampling"
        GetX0["Get x_0 from prior<br/>Already sampled at dataset level"]
        GetX1["Get x_1 from graph<br/>Ground truth target"]
        Interpolate["x_t = α_t·x_0 + β_t·x_1<br/>Different paths for continuous/categorical"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Path Types"
        Gaussian["Gaussian: Linear interpolation<br/>x_t = (1-t)·x_0 + t·x_1"]
        CTMC["CTMC Masked: Probabilistic masking<br/>Categorical features gradually revealed"]
    end
    
    SampleT --> ComputeWeights
    ComputeWeights --> GetX0
    GetX0 --> GetX1
    GetX1 --> Interpolate
    
    Interpolate --> Gaussian
    Interpolate --> CTMC
```

**Time distributions:**

| Distribution | Configuration | Use Case |
|--------------|---------------|----------|
| Uniform | `train_t_dist: 'uniform'` | Equal weighting across all time points |
| Beta | `train_t_dist: 'beta'`, `t_alpha: 1.8` | More samples near t=1 (challenging regions) |

**Conditional path functions** are modality-specific and defined in `omtra/models/conditional_paths/`. The `InterpolantScheduler` [omtra/models/interpolant_scheduler.py]() computes α_t and β_t for each modality.

**Sources:** [omtra/models/omtra.py:177-185](), [omtra/models/omtra.py:542-600](), [omtra/models/omtra.py:387-388]()

## Loss Computation

The forward pass computes multiple losses that are aggregated:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Flow Matching Losses"
        PredDst["VectorField predicts<br/>destinations dst_dict"]
        GetTargets["Extract targets x_1<br/>from graph"]
        
        ContLoss["Continuous features:<br/>MSE(prediction, target)"]
        CatLoss["Categorical features:<br/>CrossEntropy(logits, target)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Loss Modulation"
        TimeScale["Time-scaled loss?<br/>weight = 1/(1-t)²"]
        CatWeight["Categorical weight<br/>cat_loss_weight"]
        ZeroBOWeight["Zero bond order weight<br/>zero_bo_loss_weight"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Auxiliary Losses"
        AuxRegistry["Auxiliary loss registry<br/>aux_loss_name_to_class"]
        AuxCompute["Compute aux losses<br/>e.g. structure validation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Aggregation"
        TotalLoss["Sum all losses<br/>total_loss = Σ losses"]
    end
    
    PredDst --> GetTargets
    GetTargets --> ContLoss
    GetTargets --> CatLoss
    
    ContLoss --> TimeScale
    CatLoss --> TimeScale
    CatLoss --> CatWeight
    CatLoss --> ZeroBOWeight
    
    TimeScale --> TotalLoss
    CatWeight --> TotalLoss
    ZeroBOWeight --> TotalLoss
    
    AuxRegistry --> AuxCompute
    AuxCompute --> TotalLoss
```

### Loss Configuration

Losses are configured in the model initialization:

```python
# Main loss functions (per modality)
self.loss_fn_dict = nn.ModuleDict({
    "lig_x": nn.MSELoss(reduction="mean"),           # Positions
    "lig_a": nn.CrossEntropyLoss(reduction="mean"),  # Atom types
    "lig_c": nn.CrossEntropyLoss(reduction="mean"),  # Charges
    "lig_e": nn.CrossEntropyLoss(                    # Bond orders
        weight=zero_bo_weights,
        reduction="mean"
    ),
    ...
})

# Auxiliary losses
self.aux_loss_fn_dict = nn.ModuleDict({
    "structure_loss": StructureLoss(...),
    ...
})
```

**Loss computation details** [omtra/models/omtra.py:454-514]():

1. For each modality being generated, compute loss between prediction and target
2. Apply time scaling if `time_scaled_loss=True`: weight = 1/(1-t)²
3. Apply categorical weight if categorical feature
4. Compute auxiliary losses for applicable tasks
5. Sum all losses to get total loss

**Masking for categorical features:** During training, some categorical features may already be unmasked at time t. These are set to `ignore_index=-100` so they don't contribute to loss [omtra/models/omtra.py:436-442]().

**Sources:** [omtra/models/omtra.py:226-266](), [omtra/models/omtra.py:454-514]()

## Multi-Task Training Mechanics

Multi-task training allows a single model to learn multiple generation tasks simultaneously:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Phase System"
        PhaseConfig["task_phases in config<br/>Defines phase boundaries"]
        PhaseCalc["phase_idx = searchsorted<br/>phase_boundaries, batch_idx"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Task-Dataset Coupling"
        PMatrix["p_dataset_task[phase_idx]<br/>Shape: (n_tasks, n_datasets)"]
        Sample["Multinomial sample<br/>Get (task_idx, dataset_idx)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Task-Specific Processing"
        TaskClass["task_name_to_class<br/>Get Task object"]
        Modalities["modalities_generated<br/>modalities_fixed"]
        GraphBuild["build_edges<br/>Task-specific edge types"]
        Priors["sample_priors<br/>Task-specific distributions"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Training"
        Forward["forward(g, task_name)<br/>Task-aware processing"]
        Losses["Compute losses<br/>Only for generated modalities"]
    end
    
    PhaseConfig --> PhaseCalc
    PhaseCalc --> PMatrix
    PMatrix --> Sample
    
    Sample --> TaskClass
    TaskClass --> Modalities
    Modalities --> GraphBuild
    Modalities --> Priors
    
    GraphBuild --> Forward
    Priors --> Forward
    Forward --> Losses
```

### TaskDatasetCoupling

The `TaskDatasetCoupling` object [omtra/load/conf.py]() defines:

- `task_space`: List of task names (e.g., `["denovo_ligand", "fixed_protein_ligand"]`)
- `dataset_space`: List of dataset names (e.g., `["plinder", "pharmit"]`)
- `p_dataset_task`: Probability tensor of shape `(n_phases, n_tasks, n_datasets)`
- `phase_durations`: Number of steps per phase

**Example configuration:**

```yaml
task_phases:
  phase_1:
    duration: 50000
    tasks:
      denovo_ligand:
        datasets:
          pharmit: 0.7
          plinder: 0.3
  phase_2:
    duration: 50000
    tasks:
      fixed_protein_ligand:
        datasets:
          plinder: 1.0
```

This creates a training schedule where the first 50k steps sample mostly from `denovo_ligand` task, then switch to `fixed_protein_ligand`.

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/samplers.py:58-77](), [omtra/load/conf.py]()

## Checkpointing and Logging

### Manual Checkpointing

OMTRA implements custom checkpointing [omtra/models/omtra.py:201-224]():

- Saves checkpoint every `checkpoint_interval` steps (default: 1000)
- Keeps only `k_checkpoints` most recent checkpoints (default: 20)
- Saves to `{run_dir}/checkpoints/batch_{batch_idx}.ckpt`

### WandB Logging

Training metrics are logged to Weights & Biases:

```python
# Per-step metrics
self.log_dict({
    "lig_x_train_loss": loss_x,
    "lig_a_train_loss": loss_a,
    ...
}, on_step=True)

# Sample counts per task-dataset pair
self.log(
    f"{task_name}_{dataset_name}_sample_count",
    self.sample_counts[(task_name, dataset_name)],
    rank_zero_only=True
)
```

**Resume information** is saved to `resume_info.yaml` [routines/train.py:128-136]() containing:
- `run_id`: WandB run identifier
- `name`: Human-readable run name
- `url`: Link to WandB dashboard

**Sources:** [omtra/models/omtra.py:201-224](), [omtra/models/omtra.py:280-320](), [routines/train.py:113-143]()

## Validation During Training

Validation is performed periodically using `validation_step` [omtra/models/omtra.py:324-383]():

1. **Sample generation**: Generate molecules using `self.sample()`
   - For unconditional tasks: generate `2*batch_size` samples
   - For conditional tasks: generate 2 replicates per input
2. **Evaluation**: Run configured evaluation functions (if `eval_config` provided)
3. **Logging**: Log evaluation metrics to WandB

**Validation frequency** is controlled by the `val_check_interval` in the trainer configuration.

**Sources:** [omtra/models/omtra.py:324-383]()

## Configuration Summary

Key training hyperparameters from [configs/config.yaml:1-42]():

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `max_steps` | 1000 | Total training steps |
| `edges_per_batch` | 300000 | Maximum edges per batch |
| `num_workers` | 2 | DataLoader workers |
| `fake_atom_p` | 0.3 | Fraction of fake atoms to add |
| `distort_p` | 0.2 | Probability of coordinate distortion |
| `lr_warmup_steps` | 0 | Learning rate warmup duration |
| `train_t_dist` | 'uniform' | Time sampling distribution |
| `time_scaled_loss` | False | Enable time-weighted losses |
| `cat_loss_weight` | 1.0 | Weight for categorical losses |
| `zero_bo_loss_weight` | 1.0 | Weight for zero bond order class |

**Sources:** [configs/config.yaml:1-42](), [omtra/models/omtra.py:56-186]()

# Page: Training Pipeline Overview

# Training Pipeline Overview

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [configs/config.yaml](configs/config.yaml)
- [omtra/dataset/chunk_tracker.py](omtra/dataset/chunk_tracker.py)
- [omtra/dataset/data_module.py](omtra/dataset/data_module.py)
- [omtra/dataset/multitask.py](omtra/dataset/multitask.py)
- [omtra/dataset/samplers.py](omtra/dataset/samplers.py)
- [routines/train.py](routines/train.py)

</details>



This document provides a high-level overview of the OMTRA training pipeline, describing how the system orchestrates multi-task learning across multiple datasets. For specific details about configuration options, see [Configuration System](#7.2). For details about multi-task learning mechanics, see [Multi-Task Learning](#7.3). For loss computation details, see [Loss Functions and Objectives](#7.4).

## Purpose and Scope

The training pipeline coordinates the following responsibilities:

- Loading and validating Hydra configuration files
- Initializing datasets, samplers, and data loaders for multi-task learning
- Constructing the OMTRA model or ligand encoder based on training mode
- Managing PyTorch Lightning training with distributed support
- Handling checkpoint creation, resumption, and logging to Weights & Biases
- Coordinating task-dataset coupling across training phases

This page focuses on the orchestration and data flow. Model architecture details are covered in [Model Architecture](#4), and dataset-specific processing is covered in [Data Processing Pipelines](#6).

## Training Entry Point

Training begins with the `omtra` CLI command, which invokes [routines/train.py:169-195](). The main entry point uses Hydra for configuration composition:

```python
@hydra.main(version_base="1.3", config_path="../configs", config_name="config")
def main(cfg: DictConfig):
    # Handle resumption or fresh training
    # Merge task specifications
    # Call train(cfg)
```

The training script supports two primary modes specified in the configuration:

| Mode | Purpose | Model Type |
|------|---------|------------|
| `omtra` | Train the full generative model | `OMTRA` class with flow matching |
| `ligand_encoder` | Train only the VQ-VAE encoder | `LigandEncoder` class |

**Sources:** [routines/train.py:55-91](), [configs/config.yaml:15]()

## Training Pipeline Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB

    end

        TaskSampler["MultiTaskSampler<br/>omtra/dataset/samplers.py"]
        ChunkTracker["GraphChunkTracker<br/>omtra/dataset/chunk_tracker.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Initialization"
        QuickLoad["quick_load module<br/>omtra/load/quick.py"]
        OMTRAModel["OMTRA Model<br/>omtra/models/omtra.py"]
        LigEncoder["LigandEncoder<br/>omtra/models/ligand_encoder.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Training Orchestration"
        PLTrainer["PyTorch Lightning Trainer"]
        WandbLogger["WandbLogger<br/>Experiment tracking"]
        Callbacks["Callbacks<br/>Checkpointing, validation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Training Loop"

    end

    Callbacks --> PLTrainer
    
    PLTrainer --> FitLoop
    FitLoop --> SaveCkpt
```

**Sources:** [routines/train.py:1-195](), [omtra/dataset/data_module.py:1-143]()

## Core Training Components

### Configuration Loading

The training script uses Hydra's composition system to merge multiple configuration files:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Configuration Composition"
        BaseConfig["config.yaml<br/>Base configuration"]
        ModelConfig["model/default.yaml<br/>Model architecture"]
        TaskGroup["task_group/*.yaml<br/>Task definitions"]
        GraphConfig["graph/default.yaml<br/>Graph construction"]
        PriorConfig["prior/*.yaml<br/>Prior distributions"]
        TrainerConfig["trainer/default.yaml<br/>Lightning trainer"]
    end
    
    BaseConfig --> MergedConfig["Merged DictConfig"]
    ModelConfig --> MergedConfig
    TaskGroup --> MergedConfig
    GraphConfig --> MergedConfig
    PriorConfig --> MergedConfig
    TrainerConfig --> MergedConfig
    
    MergedConfig --> TaskSpecMerge["merge_task_spec()<br/>Resolve task-dataset coupling"]
    TaskSpecMerge --> FinalConfig["Final Configuration"]
```

Key configuration parameters in [configs/config.yaml:1-42]():

| Parameter | Purpose | Default |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| `mode` | Training mode (omtra/ligand_encoder) | `omtra` |
| `seed` | Random seed for reproducibility | `42` |
| `edges_per_batch` | Maximum edges per training batch | `300000` |
| `num_workers` | DataLoader worker processes | `2` |
| `max_steps` | Total training steps | `1000` |
| `fake_atom_p` | Probability bound for fake atom augmentation | `0.3` |
| `plinder_pskip_factor` | Plinder cluster-weighted sampling | `0.0` |

**Sources:** [configs/config.yaml:1-42](), [omtra/load/conf.py]()

### Data Module Initialization

The `MultiTaskDataModule` is a PyTorch Lightning data module that manages all aspects of data loading:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "MultiTaskDataModule Components"
        Init["__init__()<br/>Store configurations"]
        Setup["setup(stage='fit')<br/>Initialize datasets"]
        TrainDS["train_dataset<br/>MultitaskDataSet"]
        ValDS["val_dataset<br/>MultitaskDataSet"]
        TrainSampler["train_sampler<br/>MultiTaskSampler"]
        ValSampler["val_sampler<br/>MultiTaskSampler"]
        TrainLoader["train_dataloader()<br/>Returns DataLoader"]
        ValLoader["val_dataloader()<br/>Returns DataLoader"]
    end
    
    Init --> Setup
    Setup --> TrainDS
    Setup --> ValDS
    Setup --> TrainSampler
    Setup --> ValSampler
    TrainDS --> TrainLoader
    ValDS --> ValLoader
    TrainSampler --> TrainLoader
    ValSampler --> ValLoader
```

The data module initialization in [omtra/dataset/data_module.py:17-46]() requires:

- `dataset_config`: Paths and settings for individual datasets (Plinder, Pharmit, etc.)
- `task_phases`: Phase-based probability distributions over tasks
- `dataset_task_coupling`: Which datasets can serve which tasks
- `graph_config`: Graph construction parameters
- `prior_config`: Prior distribution specifications
- `edges_per_batch`: Batch size constraint
- `max_steps`: Number of training steps (used by sampler)

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/data_module.py:15-80](), [routines/train.py:73]()

### Model Instantiation

Model loading is handled by the `quick_load` module based on training mode:

```python
# For OMTRA training mode
if mode == 'omtra':
    if partial_ckpt:
        model = quick_load.omtra_from_partial_checkpoint(cfg, partial_ckpt)
    else:
        model = quick_load.omtra_from_config(cfg)

# For ligand encoder training mode  
elif mode == 'ligand_encoder':
    model = quick_load.lig_encoder_from_config(cfg)
```

The model initialization validates that:
- If using latent ligand generation, a `ligand_encoder_checkpoint` is specified
- All modality configurations are consistent with the selected tasks
- Prior distributions are properly configured for all generated modalities

**Sources:** [routines/train.py:76-90]()

## Multi-Task Data Loading Pipeline

The data loading pipeline implements efficient multi-task sampling with edge-aware batching:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Batch Construction Flow"
        SampleTask["MultiTaskSampler.sample_task_and_dataset()<br/>Sample (task_idx, dataset_idx) pair"]
        GetTracker["Get GraphChunkTracker<br/>for task-dataset pair"]
        GetBatch["ChunkTracker.get_batch_idxs()<br/>Adaptive batch selection"]
        FetchGraphs["MultitaskDataSet.__getitem__()<br/>Fetch DGL graphs"]
        Collate["omtra_collate_fn()<br/>Batch graphs with dgl.batch()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Chunk Management"
        ChunkIndex["chunk_index<br/>Preprocessed size metadata"]
        ChunkQueue["chunk_queue<br/>Randomized chunk order"]
        AdaptiveLoader["adaptive_batch_loader()<br/>Edge-constrained sampling"]
    end
    
    SampleTask --> GetTracker
    GetTracker --> GetBatch
    GetBatch --> ChunkIndex
    GetBatch --> ChunkQueue
    ChunkQueue --> AdaptiveLoader
    AdaptiveLoader --> FetchGraphs
    FetchGraphs --> Collate
```

### Task and Dataset Sampling

At each training step, the `MultiTaskSampler` determines which task and dataset to sample from based on the current training phase:

1. **Phase Determination**: Check `batch_idx` against `phase_boundaries` to find current phase [omtra/dataset/samplers.py:58-76]()
2. **Probability Matrix**: Use `p_dataset_task[phase_idx]` to get task-dataset probabilities for current phase
3. **Multinomial Sampling**: Draw a single (task, dataset) pair from the flattened probability distribution
4. **Distributed Broadcasting**: If distributed training, rank 0 broadcasts the sampled pair to all workers

### Adaptive Batch Loading

The `GraphChunkTracker` implements edge-aware batch construction to maximize GPU utilization:

| Component | Purpose | Key Method |
|-----------|---------|------------|
| `chunk_index` | Precomputed graph size metadata | `retrieve_graph_chunks()` |
| `chunk_queue` | Randomized chunk traversal order | `reset_queue()` |
| `adaptive_batch_loader` | Edge-constrained graph selection | Returns indices fitting in budget |

The adaptive loader [omtra/dataset/chunk_tracker.py:72-144]():
1. Shuffles graph indices within the current chunk
2. Applies optional weighted sampling based on `pskip` probabilities
3. Computes cumulative edge counts until `edges_per_batch` is reached
4. Returns the prefix of indices that fit within the budget
5. Implements fallback logic for edge cases (too-large graphs, excessive skipping)

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/samplers.py:14-180](), [omtra/dataset/chunk_tracker.py:8-144]()

## Training Loop Execution

The training loop is orchestrated by PyTorch Lightning's `Trainer`:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Training Iteration"
        FetchBatch["DataLoader yields batch<br/>(graph, task_name, dataset_name)"]
        TrainStep["model.training_step()<br/>Forward pass + loss computation"]
        Backward["Automatic differentiation<br/>Compute gradients"]
        OptStep["optimizer.step()<br/>Update parameters"]
        LogMetrics["Log to WandbLogger"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Validation Loop"
        ValBatch["Validation DataLoader"]
        ValStep["model.validation_step()"]
        ValMetrics["Aggregate validation metrics"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Checkpoint Management"
        SaveState["Save model state"]
        SaveDataModule["Save datamodule state<br/>including sampler.batch_idx"]
        SaveOptimizer["Save optimizer state"]
        WriteCkpt["Write checkpoint file"]
    end
    
    FetchBatch --> TrainStep
    TrainStep --> Backward
    Backward --> OptStep
    OptStep --> LogMetrics
    LogMetrics --> FetchBatch
    
    OptStep -.->|Every N steps| ValBatch
    ValBatch --> ValStep
    ValStep --> ValMetrics
    
    ValMetrics -.->|Checkpoint trigger| SaveState
    SaveState --> SaveDataModule
    SaveDataModule --> SaveOptimizer
    SaveOptimizer --> WriteCkpt
```

### Training Step Components

Within each training iteration, the OMTRA model:

1. **Time Sampling**: Samples time `t` from uniform or custom distribution
2. **Conditional Path**: Interpolates between prior `x_0` and data `x_1` to get `x_t`
3. **VectorField Forward**: Predicts destination `x_1` from noisy input
4. **Loss Computation**: Calculates flow matching loss and auxiliary objectives
5. **Gradient Accumulation**: Accumulates gradients for optimizer step

The training step is implemented in the model's `training_step()` method, which receives:
- `batch`: A batched DGL heterograph with all modalities
- `task_name`: The task being trained (e.g., "denovo_ligand")
- `dataset_name`: The source dataset (e.g., "pharmit", "plinder")

**Sources:** [omtra/models/omtra.py]()

### Validation Strategy

Validation sampling differs from training:

1. **Uniform Task Distribution**: The `val_sampler` uses a uniform distribution over all tasks being trained [omtra/dataset/data_module.py:62-69]()
2. **Fixed Max Steps**: Validation runs for the same number of steps as training
3. **Metrics Aggregation**: Validation metrics are logged separately per task

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/data_module.py:109-120]()

## Checkpoint and Resumption

OMTRA implements comprehensive checkpoint management for resumption:

### Fresh Training Run

For a new training run [routines/train.py:106-143]():

1. Generate a unique `run_id` using `wandb.util.generate_id()`
2. Initialize `WandbLogger` with configuration and run_id
3. Create `resume_info.yaml` containing run_id, name, and URL
4. Create symlink in `symlink_dir` pointing to Hydra output directory

### Resuming Training

To resume training [routines/train.py:92-109]():

1. Load `resume_info.yaml` from the original run directory
2. Extract the original `run_id`
3. Set `wandb_config.resume = 'must'` to resume the W&B run
4. Load original configuration and apply CLI overrides
5. Pass `ckpt_path` to `trainer.fit()`

The checkpoint contains:
- Model weights and architecture
- Optimizer state
- Datamodule state (including `sampler.batch_idx`)
- Training step counter
- Random generator states

**Checkpoint State Dictionary Structure:**

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Checkpoint Contents"
        ModelState["model.state_dict()<br/>Model parameters"]
        OptimizerState["optimizer.state_dict()<br/>Adam moments"]
        DatamoduleState["datamodule.state_dict()<br/>sampler.batch_idx"]
        TrainerState["Lightning trainer state<br/>Step counter, epoch"]
        RNGState["Random generator states<br/>torch, numpy, python"]
    end
    
    Checkpoint["checkpoint.ckpt"] --> ModelState
    Checkpoint --> OptimizerState
    Checkpoint --> DatamoduleState
    Checkpoint --> TrainerState
    Checkpoint --> RNGState
```

The datamodule state dict is critical for exact resumption [omtra/dataset/data_module.py:122-133]():

```python
def state_dict(self):
    return {
        'train_sampler_state': self.train_sampler.state_dict(),
        'val_sampler_state': self.val_sampler.state_dict()
    }
```

The sampler's `batch_idx` determines which training phase is active, ensuring the resumed run continues with the correct task-dataset distribution.

**Sources:** [routines/train.py:92-167](), [omtra/dataset/data_module.py:122-133](), [omtra/dataset/samplers.py:174-180]()

## Distributed Training Support

The training pipeline supports distributed data parallel (DDP) training:

### Sampler Synchronization

The `MultiTaskSampler` ensures all workers sample the same task-dataset pair [omtra/dataset/samplers.py:123-146]():

1. Rank 0 samples the (task_idx, dataset_idx) pair
2. Broadcast tensors to all ranks using `torch.distributed.broadcast()`
3. Each worker uses its own dataset fraction (`frac_start`, `frac_end`)
4. Workers independently construct batches from their assigned data fraction

### Worker Initialization

Each DataLoader worker is initialized with [omtra/dataset/data_module.py:141-143]():

```python
def worker_init_fn(worker_id):
    mp.set_start_method("spawn", force=True)
```

This ensures proper multiprocessing context isolation.

### Distributed Configuration

Distributed training is enabled via trainer configuration:

| Parameter | Purpose | 
|-----------|---------|
| `strategy` | Set to `DDPStrategy` for distributed |
| `devices` | Number of GPUs to use |
| `num_nodes` | Number of compute nodes |

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/samplers.py:32-56](), [omtra/dataset/samplers.py:123-146]()

## Training Configuration Summary

The following table summarizes key training parameters and their locations:

| Parameter | Config Location | Default | Purpose |
|-----------|----------------|---------|---------|
| `mode` | `config.yaml` | `omtra` | Training mode selection |
| `seed` | `config.yaml` | `42` | Random seed |
| `max_steps` | `config.yaml` | `1000` | Training duration |
| `edges_per_batch` | `config.yaml` | `300000` | Batch size constraint |
| `num_workers` | `config.yaml` | `2` | DataLoader workers |
| `fake_atom_p` | `config.yaml` | `0.3` | Fake atom augmentation |
| `task_phases` | `task_group/*.yaml` | Varies | Phase-based task scheduling |
| `dataset_task_coupling` | `task_group/*.yaml` | Varies | Task-dataset associations |
| `learning_rate` | `model/default.yaml` | Varies | Optimizer learning rate |
| `max_epochs` | `trainer/default.yaml` | Varies | Maximum epochs (if used) |

**Sources:** [configs/config.yaml:1-42]()

# Page: Configuration System

# Configuration System

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

## Purpose and Scope

This document describes OMTRA's configuration system, which uses [Hydra](https://hydra.cc/) for structured, composable configuration management. It covers the base configuration file structure, configuration groups, how to set hyperparameters, and the multi-task configuration system that enables training on multiple tasks and datasets simultaneously.

For information about specific task definitions and modalities, see [Tasks and Modalities](#3.1). For details on the training pipeline itself, see [Training Pipeline Overview](#7.1). For multi-task learning mechanics during training, see [Multi-Task Learning](#7.3).

## Base Configuration File

The main configuration file is `config.yaml`, which uses Hydra's defaults system to compose configuration from multiple sources.

### Defaults List

```yaml
defaults:
  - _self_
  - model: default
  - ligand_encoder: none
  - trainer: default
  - task_group: protein
  - graph: default
  - prior: 
    - conformer_indep
    - denovo_permute
  - callbacks: no_checkpoint
  - wandb_conf: default
  - eval: default
```

The `defaults` list specifies which configuration files to merge. Each entry corresponds to a subdirectory under `configs/` containing YAML files:

| Configuration Group | File Location | Purpose |
|---------------------|---------------|---------|
| `model` | `configs/model/` | Model architecture parameters |
| `ligand_encoder` | `configs/ligand_encoder/` | VQ-VAE encoder configuration |
| `trainer` | `configs/trainer/` | PyTorch Lightning trainer settings |
| `task_group` | `configs/task_group/` | Task phases and dataset coupling |
| `graph` | `configs/graph/` | Graph construction parameters |
| `prior` | `configs/prior/` | Prior distribution configurations |
| `callbacks` | `configs/callbacks/` | Training callbacks |
| `wandb_conf` | `configs/wandb_conf/` | Weights & Biases logging |
| `eval` | `configs/eval/` | Evaluation settings |

**Sources:** [configs/config.yaml:1-13]()

### Global Parameters

The base configuration file defines global parameters used throughout training:

```yaml
mode: omtra              # Training mode: 'omtra' or 'ligand_encoder'
seed: 42                 # Random seed
name: i_forgot_to_name_my_run  # Run name for logging

# Batch and data loading
edges_per_batch: 300000  # Maximum edges per batch
num_workers: 2           # DataLoader worker processes
max_steps: 1000          # Total training steps

# Data augmentation
fake_atom_p: 0.3         # Upper bound on fraction of fake atoms
distort_p: 0.2           # Upper bound on fraction of atoms distorted

# Plinder-specific
plinder_pskip_factor: 0.0  # Weighted sampling factor (0=no weighting, 1=uniform)
res_id_embed_dim: 64       # Residue ID embedding dimension

# Dataset paths
pharmit_path: ${omtra_root:}/data/pharmit
plinder_path: ${omtra_root:}/data/plinder
crossdocked_path: ${omtra_root:}/data/crossdocked/internal_split0

# Output management
symlink_dir: ./wandb_symlinks
```

**Sources:** [configs/config.yaml:15-42]()

## Hydra Integration

### Configuration Resolution

OMTRA uses Hydra 1.3 for configuration management. The entry point is decorated with `@hydra.main`:

```python
@hydra.main(version_base="1.3", config_path="../configs", config_name="config")
def main(cfg: DictConfig):
    # cfg is composed from all defaults + CLI overrides
```

**Sources:** [routines/train.py:169-170]()

### Custom Resolvers

OMTRA registers a custom OmegaConf resolver `omtra_root` to enable path interpolation:

```python
OmegaConf.register_new_resolver("omtra_root", omtra_root, replace=True)
```

This allows configuration values like `${omtra_root:}/data/pharmit` to resolve to absolute paths based on the package root.

**Sources:** [routines/train.py:37]()

### Output Directory Structure

Hydra automatically creates output directories for each run:

```yaml
hydra:
  run:
    dir: ./outputs/${now:%Y-%m-%d}/${name}_${now:%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%f}
```

This creates timestamped directories like:
```
outputs/
  2024-01-15/
    my_experiment_2024-01-15_14-30-123456/
      .hydra/
        config.yaml          # Resolved configuration
        hydra.yaml           # Hydra runtime config
        overrides.yaml       # CLI overrides
      checkpoints/           # Model checkpoints
      resume_info.yaml       # WandB run ID for resuming
```

**Sources:** [configs/config.yaml:39-42](), [routines/train.py:107-143]()

```mermaid
graph TD
    Start["main() entry point"]

    MergeCLI["Merge only CLI overrides<br/>with original config"]

    Start --> LoadBase
    LoadBase --> ApplyDefaults
    ApplyDefaults --> CLIOverrides
    CLIOverrides --> CheckResume
    
    CheckResume -->|No| MergeTask
    CheckResume -->|Yes| LoadOriginal
    LoadOriginal --> MergeCLI
    MergeCLI --> MergeTask

    BuildCoupling --> PassToTrain
```

**Sources:** [routines/train.py:169-191](), [omtra/load/conf.py]() (referenced but not provided)

## Multi-Task Configuration System

The multi-task configuration system is the most complex part of OMTRA's configuration. It defines which tasks the model trains on, how they're phased during training, and how tasks are coupled with datasets.

### Task Group Configuration

Task groups are defined in `configs/task_group/` and specify:
1. **task_phases**: Training phases with different task probabilities
2. **dataset_task_coupling**: Which datasets can be used for which tasks
3. **dataset_config**: Dataset-specific parameters

Example structure (conceptual):

```yaml
task_phases:
  phases:
    - name: "phase_0"
      duration: 500  # steps
      tasks:
        denovo_ligand: 0.5
        fixed_protein_ligand: 0.3
        rigid_docking: 0.2
    - name: "phase_1"
      duration: 500
      tasks:
        denovo_ligand: 0.2
        fixed_protein_ligand: 0.5
        rigid_docking: 0.3

dataset_task_coupling:
  denovo_ligand:
    pharmit: 0.7
    plinder: 0.3
  fixed_protein_ligand:
    plinder: 1.0
  rigid_docking:
    plinder: 1.0
```

### TaskDatasetCoupling Class

The `merge_task_spec` function processes the task group configuration into a `TaskDatasetCoupling` object:

```mermaid
graph LR
    TaskPhases["task_phases config<br/>Phase durations<br/>Task probabilities"]
    DatasetCoupling["dataset_task_coupling<br/>Dataset probabilities<br/>per task"]
    
    Build["build_td_coupling()"]
    
    TDC["TaskDatasetCoupling<br/>- task_space: List[str]<br/>- dataset_space: List[str]<br/>- p_dataset_task: Tensor<br/>- phase_durations: Tensor"]
    
    MultiTaskDataset["MultitaskDataSet<br/>Uses coupling to initialize<br/>correct datasets"]
    
    MultiTaskSampler["MultiTaskSampler<br/>Uses coupling to sample<br/>tasks and datasets"]
    
    TaskPhases --> Build
    DatasetCoupling --> Build
    Build --> TDC
    
    TDC --> MultiTaskDataset
    TDC --> MultiTaskSampler
```

The `p_dataset_task` tensor has shape `(n_phases, n_tasks, n_datasets)` and represents the probability of sampling each (task, dataset) pair in each phase:

```python
# Example: 2 phases, 3 tasks, 2 datasets
p_dataset_task[phase_idx, task_idx, dataset_idx] = probability
```

**Sources:** [omtra/load/conf.py]() (referenced), [omtra/dataset/multitask.py:17-41](), [omtra/dataset/samplers.py:33-41]()

### Phase Progression

During training, the sampler determines the current phase based on `batch_idx`:

```python
phase_durations = self.td_coupling.phase_durations  # e.g., [500, 500]
phase_boundaries = phase_durations.cumsum(dim=0)    # [500, 1000]
phase_idx = torch.searchsorted(phase_boundaries, self.batch_idx, right=True).item()
```

At batch 0-499: phase_idx = 0  
At batch 500-999: phase_idx = 1

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/samplers.py:61-63]()

### Prior Configuration

Prior configurations specify initial distributions for sampling `x_0`:

```yaml
prior:
  - conformer_indep      # Independent conformer-based priors
  - denovo_permute       # Permutation-based priors for de novo generation
```

Each prior configuration file defines:
- Distribution type (gaussian, ctmc_masked, etc.)
- Per-modality settings
- Training vs. inference behavior

For details on prior distributions, see [Prior Distributions](#8.2).

**Sources:** [configs/config.yaml:8-10](), [omtra/dataset/multitask.py:35]()

## Command-Line Overrides

Hydra supports hierarchical configuration overrides via command line:

```bash
# Override top-level parameters
omtra train name=my_experiment max_steps=5000 seed=123

# Override nested parameters using dot notation
omtra train model.n_recycles=3 trainer.max_steps=10000

# Select different configuration group
omtra train task_group=protein_ligand

# Multiple overrides
omtra train edges_per_batch=500000 num_workers=4 fake_atom_p=0.5
```

### Override Syntax

| Pattern | Example | Effect |
|---------|---------|--------|
| `key=value` | `seed=42` | Set top-level parameter |
| `group=choice` | `model=large` | Select from config group |
| `nested.key=value` | `model.n_layers=6` | Override nested parameter |
| `+key=value` | `+new_param=10` | Add new parameter |
| `~key` | `~callbacks` | Remove configuration group |

**Sources:** [routines/train.py:183-185]()

---

## Configuration for Resuming Training

When resuming from a checkpoint, OMTRA preserves the original configuration:

```mermaid
graph TB
    Resume["Resume with checkpoint path"]
    LoadCkpt["Load checkpoint file"]
    FindRunDir["Extract run directory<br/>from checkpoint path"]
    LoadOrigCfg["Load .hydra/config.yaml<br/>from original run"]
    GetCLI["Get current CLI overrides<br/>from HydraConfig"]
    Merge["Merge: original + CLI only"]
    RestoreState["Restore model, optimizer,<br/>sampler state"]
    
    Resume --> LoadCkpt
    LoadCkpt --> FindRunDir
    FindRunDir --> LoadOrigCfg
    LoadOrigCfg --> GetCLI
    GetCLI --> Merge
    Merge --> RestoreState
```

The resume logic ensures that only explicitly provided CLI overrides modify the configuration, preventing unintended changes:

```python
if resume:
    ckpt_path = Path(cfg.checkpoint)
    run_dir = ckpt_path.parent.parent
    original_cfg_path = run_dir / ".hydra/config.yaml"
    original_cfg = OmegaConf.load(original_cfg_path)
    overrides = HydraConfig.get().overrides.task
    cli_cfg = OmegaConf.from_dotlist(overrides)
    cfg = OmegaConf.merge(original_cfg, cli_cfg)
```

### Resume Metadata

OMTRA stores resume information in `resume_info.yaml`:

```yaml
run_id: abc123def456      # WandB run ID
name: protein_docking_001 # Run name
url: https://wandb.ai/... # WandB URL
```

This enables:
1. Resuming WandB logging to the same run
2. Creating symlinks for easy run lookup
3. Tracking run lineage

**Sources:** [routines/train.py:176-186](), [routines/train.py:93-144]()

## Best Practices

### Configuration Organization

1. **Use task groups** for logical groupings of related experiments
2. **Create custom model configs** for architecture variants
3. **Keep dataset paths** in environment variables or top-level config
4. **Version control** your custom configs in `configs/` subdirectories

### Experiment Management

```bash
# Name your runs meaningfully
omtra train name=protein_docking_v2_large_batch edges_per_batch=500000

# Use WandB tags via config
omtra train wandb_conf.tags='[experiment,baseline]'

# Symlinks enable easy lookup
ls wandb_symlinks/
# → protein_docking_v2_abc123/
```

### Multi-Phase Training Strategy

Configure task phases to implement curriculum learning:

- **Phase 0**: Focus on simpler tasks (de novo generation)
- **Phase 1**: Introduce conditional tasks (fixed protein)
- **Phase 2**: Add complex tasks (flexible docking)

**Sources:** [routines/train.py:139-143]()
