# Page: Dataset API

# Dataset API

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [notebooks/working_with_graphs.ipynb](notebooks/working_with_graphs.ipynb)
- [notebooks/zarr_dev.ipynb](notebooks/zarr_dev.ipynb)
- [notebooks/zarr_memory_investigation.ipynb](notebooks/zarr_memory_investigation.ipynb)
- [omtra/dataset/dataset.py](omtra/dataset/dataset.py)
- [omtra/dataset/pharmit.py](omtra/dataset/pharmit.py)
- [omtra/dataset/plinder.py](omtra/dataset/plinder.py)
- [omtra/dataset/zarr_dataset.py](omtra/dataset/zarr_dataset.py)
- [omtra/tasks/tasks.py](omtra/tasks/tasks.py)

</details>



This page provides a technical reference for the dataset classes and interfaces used in OMTRA. For high-level overview of available datasets and their purposes, see [Dataset Overview](#5.1). For detailed guides on using specific datasets, see [Plinder Dataset](#5.2) and [Pharmit Dataset](#5.3).

## Dataset Class Hierarchy

OMTRA uses an inheritance-based architecture for datasets, with abstract base classes providing common functionality and concrete implementations handling dataset-specific logic.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class OMTRADataset {
        <<abstract>>
        +name() str
        +__len__() int
        +__getitem__(idx) DGLHeteroGraph
        +get_num_nodes(task, start_idx, end_idx, per_ntype) int|dict
        +get_num_edges(task, start_idx, end_idx) Tensor
    }
    
    class ZarrDataset {
        <<abstract>>
        +root zarr.Group
        +store zarr.LocalStore
        +chunk_fetchers dict
        +slice_array(array_name, start_idx, end_idx) ndarray
        +build_cached_chunk_fetchers()
        +retrieve_graph_chunks(frac_start, frac_end) Tensor
    }
    
    class PlinderDataset {
        +link_version str
        +system_lookup DataFrame
        +npnde_lookup DataFrame
        +get_system(index, include_pharmacophore, include_protein, include_extra_feats, condensed_atom_typing) SystemData
        +convert_ligand(ligand, ligand_id, task, include_extra_feats, condensed_atom_typing, pocket) tuple
        +convert_protein(holo, pocket) tuple
        +convert_pharmacophore(pharmacophore) tuple
        +convert_npndes(npndes, pocket) tuple
        +encode_charges(charges) Tensor
        +infer_covalent_bonds(ligand, pocket, atom_type_map) tuple
    }
    
    class PharmitDataset {
        +n_categories_dict dict
        +retrieve_atom_idxs(idx) tuple
        +get_condensed_atom_typer() CondensedAtomTyper
    }
    
    OMTRADataset <|-- ZarrDataset
    ZarrDataset <|-- PlinderDataset
    ZarrDataset <|-- PharmitDataset
```

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/dataset.py:7-56](), [omtra/dataset/zarr_dataset.py:14-117](), [omtra/dataset/plinder.py:53-1706](), [omtra/dataset/pharmit.py:24-287]()

## Base Classes

### OMTRADataset

`OMTRADataset` is the abstract base class defining the interface all datasets must implement.

| Method | Return Type | Description |
|--------|-------------|-------------|
| `name()` | `str` | Class property returning dataset name |
| `__len__()` | `int` | Number of examples in dataset |
| `__getitem__(idx)` | `DGLHeteroGraph` | Retrieve single example as graph |
| `get_num_nodes(task, start_idx, end_idx, per_ntype=False)` | `int` or `dict` | Count nodes for batch planning |
| `get_num_edges(task, start_idx, end_idx)` | `Tensor` | Estimate edge counts for batch planning |

The `get_num_nodes()` and `get_num_edges()` methods support efficient batching by allowing the sampler to estimate graph sizes before loading them.

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/dataset.py:7-56]()

### ZarrDataset

`ZarrDataset` extends `OMTRADataset` with Zarr-specific functionality, particularly chunk-based caching for efficient data access.

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `store_path` | `Path` | Path to Zarr store |
| `store` | `zarr.LocalStore` | Zarr storage backend |
| `root` | `zarr.Group` | Root Zarr group |
| `chunk_fetchers` | `dict[str, ChunkFetcher]` | LRU cache for each array |

#### Chunk-Cached Array Access

The key innovation of `ZarrDataset` is the `slice_array()` method, which implements intelligent chunk caching:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["slice_array(array_name, start_idx, end_idx)"] --> B["Compute chunk IDs for slice"]
    B --> C["For each chunk ID"]
    C --> D{"Chunk in cache?"}
    D -->|Yes| E["Move to end (LRU)"]
    D -->|No| F["Load from disk"]
    F --> G["Evict oldest if cache full"]
    G --> H["Add to cache"]
    E --> I["Extract slice from chunk"]
    H --> I
    I --> J["Concatenate chunk slices"]
    J --> K["Return array slice"]
```

The `ChunkFetcher` class maintains an LRU cache of size `n_chunks_cache` (default 4) for each array. This significantly reduces disk I/O when accessing sequential or nearby indices.

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/zarr_dataset.py:14-117]()

## PlinderDataset

`PlinderDataset` provides access to protein-ligand complexes from the Plinder database. It supports multiple link types (holo, apo, pred) and handles complex molecular structures.

### Initialization Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `link_version` | `str` | - | Plinder link version identifier |
| `split` | `str` | - | Train/val/test split |
| `processed_data_dir` | `str` | - | Path to processed Zarr store |
| `graph_config` | `DictConfig` | `None` | Edge building configuration |
| `prior_config` | `DictConfig` | `None` | Prior sampling configuration |
| `fake_atom_p` | `float` | `0.0` | Probability of adding fake atoms |
| `pskip_factor` | `float` | `0.0` | Weighted sampling factor for clusters |
| `res_id_embed_dim` | `int` | `64` | Residue ID embedding dimension |
| `max_pharms_sampled` | `int` | `8` | Maximum pharmacophores to sample |

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/plinder.py:54-101]()

### Data Retrieval Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["__getitem__(task_name, idx)"] --> B["get_system(idx, ...)"]
    B --> C["slice_array() for each component"]
    C --> D["convert_system()"]
    D --> E["convert_ligand()"]
    D --> F["convert_protein()"]
    D --> G["convert_pharmacophore()"]
    D --> H["convert_npndes()"]
    E --> I["build_complex_graph()"]
    F --> I
    G --> I
    H --> I
    I --> J["sample_priors()"]
    J --> K["DGLHeteroGraph"]
```

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/plinder.py:1470-1706]()

### Key Methods

#### get_system()

Retrieves raw molecular data from Zarr arrays and constructs `SystemData` object.

```python
def get_system(self, index: int, 
               include_pharmacophore: bool,
               include_protein: bool,
               include_extra_feats: bool,
               condensed_atom_typing: bool) -> SystemData
```

Returns a `SystemData` containing:
- `ligand`: `LigandData` with coordinates, atom types, charges, bonds
- `receptor`: `StructureData` (full protein)
- `pocket`: `StructureData` (pocket atoms only)
- `pharmacophore`: `PharmacophoreData` (if requested)
- `npndes`: `Dict[str, LigandData]` (non-polymer entities)
- `link`: `StructureData` (apo or predicted structure if available)

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/plinder.py:172-430]()

#### Conversion Methods

The `convert_*()` methods transform raw data into graph-compatible dictionaries:

| Method | Input | Output |
|--------|-------|--------|
| `convert_ligand()` | `LigandData` | `(node_data, edge_idxs, edge_data)` |
| `convert_protein()` | `StructureData` | `(node_data, edge_idxs, edge_data, masks)` |
| `convert_pharmacophore()` | `PharmacophoreData` | `(node_data, edge_idxs, edge_data)` |
| `convert_npndes()` | `Dict[str, LigandData]` | `(node_data, edge_idxs, edge_data)` |

Each returns dictionaries with keys like:
- `node_data`: `{"lig": {"x_1_true": Tensor, "a_1_true": Tensor, ...}}`
- `edge_idxs`: `{"lig_to_lig": Tensor, ...}`
- `edge_data`: `{"lig_to_lig": {"e_1_true": Tensor}}`

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/plinder.py:667-900]()

#### Encoding Methods

PlinderDataset includes specialized encoding methods for protein features:

```python
def encode_atom_names(self, atom_names, elements, res_names) -> ndarray
def encode_elements(self, elements) -> ndarray  
def encode_res_names(self, res_names) -> ndarray
def encode_charges(self, charges) -> Tensor
```

These use vectorized lookups against predefined vocabularies (`protein_atom_map`, `protein_element_map`, `residue_map`, `charge_map`).

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/plinder.py:432-584]()

## PharmitDataset

`PharmitDataset` provides access to ligand conformers and pharmacophores from the Pharmit database. It has a simpler structure than PlinderDataset since it doesn't handle proteins.

### Initialization Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `split` | `str` | - | Train/val/test split |
| `processed_data_dir` | `str` | - | Path to processed Zarr store |
| `graph_config` | `DictConfig` | - | Edge building configuration |
| `prior_config` | `DictConfig` | - | Prior sampling configuration |
| `fake_atom_p` | `float` | `0.0` | Probability of adding fake atoms |
| `max_pharms_sampled` | `int` | `8` | Maximum pharmacophores to sample |

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/pharmit.py:24-52]()

### Data Access Pattern

PharmitDataset directly slices molecular features from Zarr arrays without intermediate conversion:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["__getitem__(task_name, idx)"] --> B["slice_array('lig/node/graph_lookup', idx)"]
    B --> C["Get start/end indices"]
    C --> D["slice_array() for x, a, c, e, edge_index"]
    D --> E{"Include pharmacophore?"}
    E -->|Yes| F["slice_array() for pharm features"]
    E -->|No| G["Build node/edge dictionaries"]
    F --> G
    G --> H["build_complex_graph()"]
    H --> I["sample_priors()"]
    I --> J["DGLHeteroGraph"]
```

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/pharmit.py:74-231]()

### Graph Chunking

PharmitDataset implements `retrieve_graph_chunks()` for distributed training support:

```python
def retrieve_graph_chunks(self, frac_start: float, frac_end: float) -> Tensor
```

Returns a `(n_chunks, 2)` tensor where each row is `[start_idx, end_idx]` for a chunk of graphs. This allows workers in distributed training to process non-overlapping subsets.

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/pharmit.py:237-260]()

## Data Structures

### Molecular Data Classes

These dataclasses (from `omtra.data.plinder`) hold raw molecular information:

| Class | Key Attributes | Purpose |
|-------|----------------|---------|
| `LigandData` | `coords`, `atom_types`, `atom_charges`, `bond_types`, `bond_indices`, `is_covalent` | Small molecule representation |
| `StructureData` | `coords`, `atom_names`, `elements`, `res_ids`, `res_names`, `chain_ids`, `backbone` | Protein structure |
| `PharmacophoreData` | `coords`, `types`, `vectors`, `interactions` | Pharmacophore features |
| `BackboneData` | `coords`, `res_ids`, `res_names`, `chain_ids` | Backbone-only representation |
| `SystemData` | `ligand`, `receptor`, `pocket`, `pharmacophore`, `npndes`, `link` | Complete complex |

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/plinder.py:26-32]()

### MolXACE Representation

The `MolXACE` class represents ligands in the XACE (x, a, c, e) format:

| Attribute | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `x` | Atomic coordinates (N, 3) |
| `a` | Atom types (N,) |
| `c` | Formal charges (N,) |
| `e` | Bond orders (E,) |
| `edge_idxs` | Bond connectivity (E, 2) |
| `cond_a` | Condensed atom types (optional) |
| `impl_H`, `aro`, `hyb`, `ring`, `chiral` | Extra features (optional) |

PharmitDataset and PlinderDataset both convert ligands to `MolXACE` format before graph construction.

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/plinder.py:680-681](), [omtra/dataset/pharmit.py:137-143]()

## Integration with Tasks

Datasets use the `Task` system to determine what data to load and how to process it:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Dataset.__getitem__(task_name, idx)"] --> B["task_name_to_class(task_name)"]
    B --> C["Task class instance"]
    C --> D{"Check task.groups_present"}
    D -->|"'pharmacophore' in groups"| E["include_pharmacophore = True"]
    D -->|"'ligand_identity_condensed' in groups"| F["condensed_atom_typing = True"]
    D -->|"'ligand_identity_extra' in groups"| G["include_extra_feats = True"]
    E --> H["Load and convert data accordingly"]
    F --> H
    G --> H
    H --> I["build_complex_graph(task=Task)"]
    I --> J["get_prior(Task, prior_config)"]
    J --> K["sample_priors(graph, Task, priors)"]
```

Tasks control:
- Which modalities are loaded (`groups_present`)
- Which modalities are fixed vs. generated (`groups_fixed`, `groups_generated`)
- Graph edge types (via `task.groups_present`)
- Prior distributions (via `task.priors`)

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/plinder.py:1470-1490](), [omtra/dataset/pharmit.py:76-88]()

## Batching Support

Datasets provide methods to support efficient batching:

### Node Counting

```python
def get_num_nodes(self, task: Task, start_idx: int, end_idx: int, per_ntype: bool = False)
```

Returns node counts for graphs `[start_idx, end_idx)`. If `per_ntype=True`, returns a dict mapping node types to counts. Used by `MultiTaskSampler` to construct batches with controlled sizes.

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/pharmit.py:262-287](), [omtra/dataset/dataset.py:27-29]()

### Edge Estimation

```python
def get_num_edges(self, task: Task, start_idx: int, end_idx: int) -> Tensor
```

Estimates edge counts using `approx_n_edges()` based on graph configuration and node counts. Cached with LRU cache for performance.

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/dataset.py:32-55]()

## Weighted Sampling (PlinderDataset)

PlinderDataset supports cluster-based weighted sampling controlled by `pskip_factor`:

- `pskip_factor = 0.0`: Uniform sampling
- `pskip_factor = 1.0`: Sample uniformly across clusters (downweight large clusters)

When enabled, the `system_lookup` DataFrame gains a `pskip` column with skip probabilities, computed by `compute_pskip()`.

**Sources:** [omtra/dataset/plinder.py:62-93]()

---

# Page: Evaluation API

# Evaluation API

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [configs/eval/default.yaml](configs/eval/default.yaml)
- [notebooks/docking_evaluation.ipynb](notebooks/docking_evaluation.ipynb)
- [omtra/data/graph/utils.py](omtra/data/graph/utils.py)
- [omtra/eval/evals.py](omtra/eval/evals.py)
- [omtra/eval/system.py](omtra/eval/system.py)
- [omtra/eval/utils.py](omtra/eval/utils.py)
- [omtra_pipelines/docking_eval/docking_eval.py](omtra_pipelines/docking_eval/docking_eval.py)
- [omtra_pipelines/docking_eval/gen_eval_cmds.py](omtra_pipelines/docking_eval/gen_eval_cmds.py)
- [omtra_pipelines/docking_eval/sampleblaster.py](omtra_pipelines/docking_eval/sampleblaster.py)
- [routines/sample.py](routines/sample.py)

</details>



This page documents the API for evaluating generated molecular systems in OMTRA. The evaluation API consists of the `SampledSystem` class for converting DGL graphs to evaluation-ready formats, a collection of registered evaluation functions for computing metrics, and utility functions for specific metric calculations.

For information about the sampling process that produces systems to evaluate, see [Sampling and Inference](#8). For details on the docking evaluation pipeline script, see [Docking Evaluation Pipeline](#9.2).

## Overview

The evaluation API provides three main components:

1. **`SampledSystem` class** - Converts DGL heterogeneous graphs into molecular formats (RDKit molecules, Biotite atom arrays) suitable for evaluation
2. **Registered evaluation functions** - Task-specific metric computation functions decorated with `@register_eval`
3. **Docking evaluation utilities** - Comprehensive evaluation pipeline with PoseBusters, GNINA, PoseCheck, and pharmacophore matching

The evaluation workflow typically follows this pattern:

```mermaid
graph LR
    G["DGL HeteroGraph<br/>(from sampling)"]
    SS["SampledSystem<br/>omtra/eval/system.py"]
    RDKit["RDKit Mol"]
    Biotite["Biotite AtomArray"]
    Metrics["Metrics Dict"]
    
    G --> SS
    SS --> RDKit
    SS --> Biotite
    RDKit --> Metrics
    Biotite --> Metrics
```

**Sources:** [omtra/eval/system.py:1-1000](), [routines/sample.py:1-503]()

## SampledSystem Class

The `SampledSystem` class is the central interface for converting generated molecular systems into evaluation-ready formats. It handles both ligands and proteins, supporting various atom typing schemes including condensed atom types.

### Class Structure

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "SampledSystem Initialization"
        Init["__init__<br/>omtra/eval/system.py:43-95"]
        G_Input["g: DGL HeteroGraph"]
        Task["task: Task"]
        Typer["cond_a_typer: CondensedAtomTyper"]
        
        G_Input --> Init
        Task --> Init
        Typer --> Init
    end
    
    subgraph "Molecular Extraction Methods"
        GetLig["get_rdkit_ligand()<br/>Returns RDKit Mol"]
        GetGTLig["get_gt_ligand()<br/>Returns ground truth Mol"]
        GetProt["get_rdkit_protein()<br/>Returns RDKit Mol"]
        GetProtArr["get_protein_array()<br/>Returns Biotite AtomArray"]
        GetPharm["get_pharmacophore_from_graph()<br/>Returns pharmacophore dict"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Extraction"
        ExtractLig["extract_ligdata_from_graph()<br/>line:491-575"]
        ExtractProt["extract_protdata_from_graph()<br/>line:577-603"]
        BuildMol["build_molecule()<br/>line:605-644"]
        BuildArr["build_atom_array()<br/>line:327-371"]
    end
    
    Init --> GetLig
    GetLig --> ExtractLig
    ExtractLig --> BuildMol
    GetProtArr --> ExtractProt
    ExtractProt --> BuildArr
```

**Sources:** [omtra/eval/system.py:38-95](), [omtra/eval/system.py:400-450]()

### Key Methods

| Method | Return Type | Description |
|--------|-------------|-------------|
| `get_rdkit_ligand()` | `Chem.Mol` | Returns generated ligand as RDKit molecule |
| `get_gt_ligand()` | `Chem.Mol` | Returns ground truth ligand from graph |
| `get_rdkit_ref_ligand()` | `Chem.Mol` | Returns reference ligand (for comparison) |
| `get_rdkit_protein()` | `Chem.Mol` | Returns generated protein as RDKit molecule |
| `get_protein_array()` | `struc.AtomArray` | Returns protein as Biotite AtomArray |
| `get_pharmacophore_from_graph()` | `Dict` | Returns pharmacophore coordinates and types |
| `get_n_lig_atoms()` | `int` | Returns number of ligand atoms (excluding fake) |
| `write_ligand()` | `None` | Writes ligand to SDF file |
| `write_protein()` | `None` | Writes protein to CIF/PDB file |

**Sources:** [omtra/eval/system.py:128-450]()

### Internal Data Extraction

The `SampledSystem` class extracts molecular data from DGL graphs in two stages:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Graph Features"
        NodeX["Node: x_1<br/>(coordinates)"]
        NodeA["Node: a_1<br/>(atom types)"]
        NodeC["Node: c_1<br/>(charges)"]
        EdgeE["Edge: e_1<br/>(bond types)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "extract_ligdata_from_graph"
        ExtractPos["Extract positions"]
        MapAtoms["Map atom type indices<br/>to element symbols"]
        MapCharges["Map charge indices<br/>to formal charges"]
        FilterBonds["Filter upper triangle<br/>+ non-zero bonds"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Tuple"
        OutPos["positions: Tensor"]
        OutAtoms["atom_types: List[str]"]
        OutCharges["atom_charges: List[int]"]
        OutBonds["bond_types: Tensor"]
        OutSrc["bond_src_idxs: Tensor"]
        OutDst["bond_dst_idxs: Tensor"]
    end
    
    NodeX --> ExtractPos
    NodeA --> MapAtoms
    NodeC --> MapCharges
    EdgeE --> FilterBonds
    
    ExtractPos --> OutPos
    MapAtoms --> OutAtoms
    MapCharges --> OutCharges
    FilterBonds --> OutBonds
    FilterBonds --> OutSrc
    FilterBonds --> OutDst
```

**Sources:** [omtra/eval/system.py:491-575](), [omtra/data/graph/utils.py:36-38]()

### Molecule Construction

The `build_molecule` method constructs RDKit molecules from extracted graph data:

**Key Steps:**
1. Create empty `RWMol` object
2. Add atoms with element types and formal charges
3. Add bonds between atoms using upper triangle indices
4. Set 3D coordinates from positions tensor
5. Convert to immutable `Mol` object

**Sources:** [omtra/eval/system.py:605-644]()

### Condensed Atom Type Decoding

For tasks using condensed atom types (e.g., `ligand_identity_condensed`), the class automatically decodes them:

```mermaid
graph TB
    HasCond{"has_condensed_typing?"}
    Decode["decode_conda()<br/>line:96-117"]
    CondTyper["cond_a_typer.cond_a_to_feats()"]
    SetFeats["Set a_1, c_1 features<br/>from condensed type"]
    
    HasCond -->|Yes| Decode
    Decode --> CondTyper
    CondTyper --> SetFeats
```

**Sources:** [omtra/eval/system.py:87-117]()

## Built-in Evaluation Functions

OMTRA provides a set of registered evaluation functions that can be applied to lists of `SampledSystem` objects. These are registered using the `@register_eval` decorator and configured per-task in [configs/eval/default.yaml]().

### Evaluation Function Registry

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Registration System"
        Decorator["@register_eval(name)<br/>omtra/eval/register.py"]
        Registry["EVAL_REGISTRY dict"]
        GetEval["get_eval(name)<br/>Returns function"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Evaluation Functions"
        Valid["@register_eval('validity')<br/>compute_validity()"]
        Stable["@register_eval('stability')<br/>compute_stability()"]
        Geom["@register_eval('geometry')<br/>geometry()"]
        RMSD["@register_eval('ligand_rmsd')<br/>ligand_rmsd()"]
        PB["@register_eval('pb_valid_unconditional')<br/>pb_valid_unconditional()"]
        Pharm["@register_eval('pharm_match')<br/>check_pharm_match()"]
    end
    
    Valid --> Decorator
    Stable --> Decorator
    Geom --> Decorator
    Decorator --> Registry
    Registry --> GetEval
```

**Sources:** [omtra/eval/evals.py:1-329]()

### Available Metrics

| Metric Name | Function | Description | Key Output |
|-------------|----------|-------------|------------|
| `validity` | `validity()` | RDKit sanitization and connectivity | `frac_valid_mols`, `frac_connected` |
| `stability` | `stability()` | Atom valence stability | `frac_atoms_stable`, `frac_mols_stable_valence` |
| `reos_and_rings` | `check_reos_and_rings()` | REOS filter violations and OOD ring systems | `flag_rate`, `ood_rate` |
| `geometry` | `geometry()` | Bond length/angle validity | `geometry_frac_valid_bonds`, `geometry_frac_valid_angles` |
| `flatness` | `flatness()` | Aromatic ring planarity | `flatness_max_distance_from_plane` |
| `intermolecular_distance` | `intermolecular_distance()` | Ligand-protein clash detection | `intermolecular_distance_smallest` |
| `ligand_rmsd` | `ligand_rmsd()` | RMSD to ground truth | `ligand_rmsd`, `ligand_kabsch_rmsd` |
| `volume_overlap` | `volume_overlap()` | Protein-ligand overlap | `volume_overlap` |
| `pb_valid_unconditional` | `pb_valid_unconditional()` | PoseBusters validation (no protein) | `pb_valid`, individual PB checks |
| `pb_valid_pocket` | `pb_valid_pocket()` | PoseBusters validation (with protein) | `pb_valid_pocket` |
| `pb_valid_conformer` | `pb_valid_conformer()` | PoseBusters conformer validation | `pb_conformer_*` metrics |
| `pharm_match` | `check_pharm_match()` | Pharmacophore matching | `perfect_pharm_match`, `frac_true_pharms_matched` |

**Sources:** [omtra/eval/evals.py:37-329](), [configs/eval/default.yaml:1-684]()

### Usage Pattern

```python
from omtra.eval.register import get_eval

# Get evaluation function
validity_fn = get_eval("validity")

# Compute metrics on list of SampledSystem objects
metrics = validity_fn(sampled_systems, params={})
# Returns: {"frac_valid_mols": 0.95, "frac_connected": 0.92, ...}
```

**Sources:** [routines/sample.py:483-497]()

## Utility Functions

The [omtra/eval/utils.py]() file provides lower-level utility functions used by the registered evaluation functions.

### Validity Computation

```mermaid
graph TB
    Input["List[SampledSystem]"]
    Loop["For each system"]
    GetMol["sys.get_rdkit_ligand()"]
    Sanitize["Chem.SanitizeMol()"]
    Frags["Chem.GetMolFrags()"]
    
    Valid{"Valid?"}
    Connected{"Connected?"}
    
    Counts["Count valid/connected<br/>Track error types"]
    Metrics["frac_valid_mols<br/>frac_connected<br/>avg_num_components"]
    
    Input --> Loop
    Loop --> GetMol
    GetMol --> Sanitize
    Sanitize --> Valid
    Valid -->|Yes| Frags
    Frags --> Connected
    Valid -->|No| Counts
    Connected --> Counts
    Counts --> Metrics
```

**Sources:** [omtra/eval/utils.py:25-106]()

### Stability Computation

Validates atom valencies against a pre-computed valency table:

**Key Functions:**
- `compute_stability()` - Computes fraction of stable atoms/molecules
- `check_stability()` - Validates individual molecule valencies
- `get_valid_valency_table()` - Loads allowed valencies from YAML

**Sources:** [omtra/eval/utils.py:109-192]()

### REOS and Ring System Analysis

```mermaid
graph LR
    Systems["List[SampledSystem]"]
    Extract["Extract RDKit mols<br/>Sanitize"]
    
    subgraph "REOS Analysis"
        REOS["REOS class<br/>Glaxo + Dundee rules"]
        Flags["Count filter violations"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Ring Analysis"
        Counter["RingSystemCounter"]
        Compare["Compare to ChEMBL<br/>distribution"]
        OOD["Count OOD rings"]
    end
    
    Systems --> Extract
    Extract --> REOS
    Extract --> Counter
    REOS --> Flags
    Counter --> Compare
    Compare --> OOD
```

**Sources:** [omtra/eval/utils.py:194-239]()

### PoseBusters Integration

The utility functions provide wrappers for PoseBusters validation:

- `bust_redock()` - For cognate receptor docking
- `bust_dock()` - For de novo or non-cognate docking
- `bust_mol()` - For molecule-only validation

**Sources:** [omtra/eval/utils.py:279-337]()

## Docking Evaluation Pipeline

The [omtra_pipelines/docking_eval/docking_eval.py]() script provides a comprehensive evaluation pipeline that combines sampling, file writing, and metric computation.

### Pipeline Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input"
        Ckpt["Checkpoint Path<br/>or Samples Dir"]
        Task["Task Name"]
        Dataset["Dataset<br/>(plinder/crossdocked)"]
        SysIdxs["System Indices"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Sampling Phase"
        Sample["sample_system()<br/>line:537-657"]
        ModelSample["model.sample_in_batches()"]
        GList["g_list: DGL graphs"]
        SS["sampled_systems:<br/>List[SampledSystem]"]
    end
    
    subgraph "File Writing"
        WritePairs["write_system_pairs()<br/>line:661-777"]
        Proteins["PDB files"]
        Ligands["SDF files"]
        Pharm["Pharmacophore XYZ"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Metrics Computation"
        Compute["compute_metrics()<br/>line:332-534"]
        PB["PoseBusters"]
        GNINA["GNINA scoring"]
        PC["PoseCheck"]
        RMSD_M["RMSD"]
        PharmMatch["Pharmacophore matching"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        CSV["eval_metrics.csv"]
    end
    
    Ckpt --> Sample
    Task --> Sample
    Dataset --> Sample
    SysIdxs --> Sample
    
    Sample --> ModelSample
    ModelSample --> GList
    ModelSample --> SS
    
    GList --> WritePairs
    SS --> WritePairs
    WritePairs --> Proteins
    WritePairs --> Ligands
    WritePairs --> Pharm
    
    Proteins --> Compute
    Ligands --> Compute
    Task --> Compute
    
    Compute --> PB
    Compute --> GNINA
    Compute --> PC
    Compute --> RMSD_M
    Compute --> PharmMatch
    
    PB --> CSV
    GNINA --> CSV
    PC --> CSV
    RMSD_M --> CSV
    PharmMatch --> CSV
```

**Sources:** [omtra_pipelines/docking_eval/docking_eval.py:1-1400]()

### Key Pipeline Functions

| Function | Lines | Description |
|----------|-------|-------------|
| `parse_args()` | 39-94 | Argument parsing for sampling/evaluation options |
| `sample_system()` | 537-657 | Loads model, dataset, and generates samples |
| `write_system_pairs()` | 661-777 | Writes generated and ground truth files |
| `system_pairs_from_path()` | 780-868 | Loads existing samples from directory |
| `compute_metrics()` | 332-534 | Computes all requested metrics |

**Sources:** [omtra_pipelines/docking_eval/docking_eval.py:39-868]()

### Metric Functions

The pipeline includes specialized metric computation functions:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "PoseBusters Validation"
        PBValid["pb_valid()<br/>line:97-121"]
        Config["'dock' or 'redock'<br/>configuration"]
        PBDf["DataFrame with<br/>individual checks"]
    end
    
    subgraph "GNINA Scoring"
        GNINA["gnina()<br/>line:183-195"]
        ScoreOnly["Score only mode"]
        Minimize["Minimization mode"]
        Scores["minimizedAffinity<br/>CNNscore<br/>CNNaffinity"]
    end
    
    subgraph "PoseCheck Analysis"
        PC["posecheck()<br/>line:198-245"]
        Clashes["Clash detection"]
        Strain["Strain energy"]
        Interactions["Interaction fingerprints"]
        Recovery["Interaction recovery"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Other Metrics"
        RMSD["rmsd()<br/>line:248-252"]
        PharmMatch["compute_pharmacophore_match()<br/>line:255-292"]
    end
```

**Sources:** [omtra_pipelines/docking_eval/docking_eval.py:97-292]()

### System Pairs Structure

The pipeline organizes data into "system pairs" for evaluation:

```python
system_pairs = {
    'sys_0_gt': {
        'pair_0': {
            'gen_ligs': [rdkit_mol, ...],          # Generated ligands
            'gen_ligs_file': Path('gen_ligands.sdf'),
            'gen_ligs_ids': ['gen_ligands_0', ...],
            'true_lig': rdkit_mol,                  # Ground truth ligand
            'true_lig_file': Path('ligand.sdf'),
            'gen_prot_file': Path('protein_0.pdb'), # Generated protein
            'gen_prot_id': 'protein_0',
            'true_prot_file': Path('protein_0.pdb'),# Ground truth protein
            'true_prot_id': 'protein_0',
            'true_pharm': {...}                     # Pharmacophore dict
        }
    }
}
```

**Sources:** [omtra_pipelines/docking_eval/docking_eval.py:677-776]()

### Timeout Handling

The pipeline includes timeout protection for long-running metrics:

```mermaid
graph LR
    Func["Metric Function"]

    Process["Multiprocessing"]
    
    Success["Return Result"]
    TimeoutKill["Kill Process<br/>Return None"]
    Error["Catch Exception<br/>Return None"]
    
    Func --> Timeout
    Timeout --> Process
    Process --> Success
    Process --> TimeoutKill
    Process --> Error
```

**Sources:** [omtra_pipelines/docking_eval/docking_eval.py:295-318]()

## Output Formats

### File Writing Functions

The `SampledSystem` class provides methods to write molecules to standard file formats:

| Method | File Format | Description |
|--------|-------------|-------------|
| `write_ligand()` | SDF | Writes ligand to SDF file via `write_mols_to_sdf()` |
| `write_protein()` | CIF | Writes protein to CIF file via `write_arrays_to_cif()` |
| `write_protein_pdb()` | PDB | Writes protein to PDB file via `write_arrays_to_pdb()` |
| `write_pharmacophore()` | XYZ | Writes pharmacophore points with element labels |

**Sources:** [omtra/eval/system.py:733-830]()

## Configuration

Evaluation metrics are configured per-task in [configs/eval/default.yaml](). Each task specifies which metrics to run and their parameters:

```yaml
rigid_docking_condensed:
  - stability:
      train: true
      params: {}
  - reos_and_rings:
      train: true
      params: {}
  - intermolecular_distance:
      train: true
      params:
        clash_cutoff: 0.05
  - ligand_rmsd:
      train: true
      params:
        rmsd_threshold: 2.0
  - pb_valid_unconditional:
      train: true
      params:
        max_workers: 0
```

**Sources:** [configs/eval/default.yaml:180-206]()

## Usage Examples

### Basic Evaluation in Sampling Script

```python
# From routines/sample.py
from omtra.eval.register import get_eval

# Load evaluation configuration
default_eval_cfg = OmegaConf.load('configs/eval/default.yaml')

metrics = {}
for eval_entry in default_eval_cfg[task_name]:
    for eval_name, config in eval_entry.items():
        # Get registered evaluation function
        eval_fn = get_eval(eval_name)
        # Compute metrics
        result = eval_fn(sampled_systems, config.get("params", {}))
        metrics.update(result)

# Write metrics to file
with open('metrics.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(metrics, f)
```

**Sources:** [routines/sample.py:483-497]()

### Comprehensive Docking Evaluation

```bash
python omtra_pipelines/docking_eval/docking_eval.py \
  --ckpt_path /path/to/checkpoint.ckpt \
  --task rigid_docking_condensed \
  --dataset plinder \
  --n_samples 100 \
  --n_replicates 5 \
  --n_timesteps 250 \
  --output_dir /path/to/output
```

**Sources:** [omtra_pipelines/docking_eval/docking_eval.py:39-94]()

### Converting Graph to RDKit Molecule

```python
from omtra.eval.system import SampledSystem
from omtra.data.condensed_atom_typing import CondensedAtomTyper

# Create SampledSystem from DGL graph
cond_a_typer = CondensedAtomTyper(fake_atoms=False)
sys = SampledSystem(
    g=graph,
    task=task,
    fake_atoms=False,
    cond_a_typer=cond_a_typer
)

# Get RDKit molecule
rdkit_mol = sys.get_rdkit_ligand()

# Get ground truth for comparison
gt_mol = sys.get_gt_ligand(g=graph)

# Get protein as Biotite AtomArray
protein_arr = sys.get_protein_array()
```

**Sources:** [omtra/eval/system.py:38-450]()

# Graph and Prior APIs

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

- [omtra/data/graph/__init__.py](omtra/data/graph/__init__.py)

- [omtra/data/graph/edge_factory.py](omtra/data/graph/edge_factory.py)
- [omtra/data/graph/register.py](omtra/data/graph/register.py)
- [omtra/priors/prior_factory.py](omtra/priors/prior_factory.py)

- [omtra/tasks/utils.py](omtra/tasks/utils.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This document provides a comprehensive API reference for graph construction and prior sampling systems in OMTRA. These APIs define how molecular systems are represented as heterogeneous graphs and how initial states (`x_0`) are sampled from prior distributions during generation.

For conceptual understanding of graph representations, see [Graph Representation](#3.3). For information on how graphs are constructed from dataset files, see [Graph Construction](#5.5). For task-specific usage of priors, see [Prior Distributions](#8.2).

This page focuses on the programmatic interfaces: function signatures, parameters, return types, and usage patterns.

---

## Graph Construction API

### Node and Edge Type Definitions

OMTRA uses a fixed set of node and edge types defined in [omtra/data/graph/\_\_init\_\_.py:13-18]().

**Node Types:**
```python
node_types = ['lig', 'prot_atom', 'prot_res', 'pharm', 'npnde']
```

**Edge Type Naming Convention:**

| Pattern | Example | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `{ntype}_to_{ntype}` | `lig_to_lig` | Standard edges between node types |
| `{src}_covalent_{dst}` | `prot_atom_covalent_lig` | Covalent bond edges |

All edge types are enumerated in `all_edge_types` [omtra/data/graph/\_\_init\_\_.py:16-18](), including symmetric pairs.

**Canonical Edge Type Format:**

The function `to_canonical_etype(etype: str)` [omtra/data/graph/\_\_init\_\_.py:20-26]() converts edge type strings to DGL's canonical tuple format `(src_ntype, etype, dst_ntype)`.

```python
# Example usage:
to_canonical_etype("lig_to_pharm")  # → ('lig', 'lig_to_pharm', 'pharm')
to_canonical_etype("prot_atom_covalent_lig")  # → ('prot_atom', 'prot_atom_covalent_lig', 'lig')
```

Sources: [omtra/data/graph/\_\_init\_\_.py:13-36]()

---

### Core Graph Construction Function

#### `build_complex_graph`

The primary function for constructing heterogeneous DGL graphs from molecular data.

**Signature:**
```python
def build_complex_graph(
    node_data: Dict[str, Dict[str, torch.Tensor]],
    edge_idxs: Dict[str, torch.Tensor],
    edge_data: Dict[str, Dict[str, torch.Tensor]],
    task: Task = None,
    graph_config: DictConfig = None,
) -> dgl.DGLHeteroGraph
```

**Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `node_data` | `Dict[str, Dict[str, torch.Tensor]]` | Nested dict: `{ntype: {feature_name: tensor}}` |
| `edge_idxs` | `Dict[str, torch.Tensor]` | Edge indices: `{etype: tensor([src_indices], [dst_indices])}` |
| `edge_data` | `Dict[str, Dict[str, torch.Tensor]]` | Nested dict: `{etype: {feature_name: tensor}}` |
| `task` | `Task` | Optional task to filter edge types |
| `graph_config` | `DictConfig` | Optional config for edge construction parameters |

**Returns:** `dgl.DGLHeteroGraph` with node and edge features attached

**Edge Type Filtering:**

When `task` and `graph_config` are provided, the function uses `get_edges_for_task(task, graph_config)` [omtra/data/graph/\_\_init\_\_.py:46-72]() to determine which edge types to include based on:
1. Node types present in the task's modalities
2. Edge types specified in `graph_config.edges`
3. Symmetric edge type declarations

**Protein Covalent Bond Inference:**

If `graph_config.cov_prot_edges` is `True` and protein atoms are present, covalent bonds are automatically inferred using a radius graph with `r=2.1 Å` [omtra/data/graph/\_\_init\_\_.py:122-137]().

Sources: [omtra/data/graph/\_\_init\_\_.py:74-155]()

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Input["Input Data Structures"]
        ND["node_data<br/>{ntype: {feat: tensor}}"]
        EI["edge_idxs<br/>{etype: tensor[2, n]}"]
        ED["edge_data<br/>{etype: {feat: tensor}}"]
        T["task: Task"]
        GC["graph_config: DictConfig"]
    end
    
    subgraph Processing["Graph Construction"]
        GEF["get_edges_for_task()"]
        NNC["Calculate num_nodes<br/>per node type"]
        ECD["Build edge_construction_dict"]
        CBI["Infer covalent bonds<br/>if cov_prot_edges=True"]
        HG["dgl.heterograph()"]
    end
    
    subgraph Output["Output Graph"]
        G["DGLHeteroGraph<br/>with node/edge features"]
    end
    
    T --> GEF
    GC --> GEF
    GEF --> ECD
    ND --> NNC
    NNC --> HG
    EI --> ECD
    ECD --> HG
    ND --> CBI
    GC --> CBI
    CBI --> HG
    HG --> G
    ND --> G
    ED --> G
    
    style GEF fill:#f9f9f9
    style HG fill:#f9f9f9
```

Sources: [omtra/data/graph/\_\_init\_\_.py:74-155]()

---

### Dynamic Edge Construction

During model execution, edges are built dynamically based on current node positions using `build_edges` and removed using `remove_edges`.

#### `build_edges`

**Signature:**
```python
def build_edges(
    g: dgl.DGLHeteroGraph, 
    task: Task, 
    node_batch_idx: Dict[str, torch.Tensor], 
    graph_config: DictConfig,
    etype_subset: List[str] = None,
    lig_only: bool = False,
) -> dgl.DGLHeteroGraph
```

**Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `g` | `dgl.DGLHeteroGraph` | Graph to add edges to |
| `task` | `Task` | Task defining valid edge types |
| `node_batch_idx` | `Dict[str, torch.Tensor]` | Batch index for each node type |
| `graph_config` | `DictConfig` | Configuration for edge builders |
| `etype_subset` | `List[str]` | Optional subset of edge types to build |
| `lig_only` | `bool` | If `True`, only build edges involving ligand nodes |

**Behavior:**
- Uses `x_t` positions from `g.nodes[ntype].data["x_t"]` [omtra/tasks/utils.py:46]()
- Skips predetermined edge types (`lig_to_lig`, `npnde_to_npnde`) [omtra/tasks/utils.py:27-28]()
- Skips covalent edges (already in graph)
- For `prot_atom_to_prot_atom`, combines radius-based edges with covalent edges [omtra/tasks/utils.py:53-54]()

#### `remove_edges`

**Signature:**
```python
def remove_edges(
    g: dgl.DGLHeteroGraph, 
    lig_only: bool = False
) -> dgl.DGLHeteroGraph
```

Removes all non-predetermined edges (inverse of `build_edges`).

Sources: [omtra/tasks/utils.py:16-107]()

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph EdgeLifecycle["Edge Lifecycle During Generation"]
        G0["Graph at t=0<br/>Static edges:<br/>lig_to_lig,<br/>npnde_to_npnde,<br/>covalent bonds"]
        
        BE["build_edges()<br/>Create spatial edges<br/>based on x_t"]
        
        G1["Graph with<br/>dynamic edges<br/>for message passing"]
        
        MP["GNN Message<br/>Passing"]
        
        RE["remove_edges()<br/>Clear spatial edges"]
        
        G2["Graph ready<br/>for next timestep"]
    end
    
    G0 --> BE
    BE --> G1
    G1 --> MP
    MP --> RE
    RE --> G2
    G2 -.->|"Update x_t"| BE
```

Sources: [omtra/tasks/utils.py:16-92]()

---

### Edge Builder Functions

Edge builders are registered functions that create edges between nodes based on spatial criteria. They are accessed via the factory pattern.

#### Registration System

**Decorator:**
```python
@register_edge_builder(name: str)
def builder_function(src_pos, dst_pos, src_batch_idx, dst_batch_idx, **params):
    ...
```

Sources: [omtra/data/graph/register.py:1-11]()

#### Built-in Edge Builders

| Builder | Registration Name | Parameters | Description |
|---------|------------------|------------|-------------|
| `complete_graph` | `"complete"` | None | Fully connected (excluding self-loops) |
| `hetero_radius` | `"radius"` | `r`, `max_num_neighbors` | Edges within radius `r` |
| `hetero_knn` | `"knn"` | `k` | K-nearest neighbors |
| `symmetric` | `"symmetric"` | `builder_fn` | Inverse edges of another builder |

**Function Signatures:**

```python
# Complete graph (all-to-all)
def complete_graph(src_pos, dst_pos, src_batch_idx, dst_batch_idx) -> torch.Tensor
    # Returns: tensor([src_indices], [dst_indices])

# Radius-based edges
def hetero_radius(
    src_pos, dst_pos, 
    src_batch_idx, dst_batch_idx, 
    r: float, 
    max_num_neighbors: int = 1000
) -> torch.Tensor

# K-nearest neighbors
def hetero_knn(
    src_pos, dst_pos, 
    src_batch_idx, dst_batch_idx, 
    k: int
) -> torch.Tensor

# Symmetric edges
def symmetric(
    builder_fn, 
    src_pos, dst_pos, 
    src_batch_idx, dst_batch_idx
) -> torch.Tensor
```

Sources: [omtra/data/graph/edge_builders.py:1-32]()

#### `get_edge_builders`

Factory function that creates edge builder functions with parameters bound.

**Signature:**
```python
@functools.lru_cache()
def get_edge_builders(graph_config: DictConfig) -> Dict[str, Callable]
```

**Returns:** Dictionary mapping edge type strings to parameterized builder functions

**Example Configuration (YAML):**
```yaml
edges:
  lig_to_pharm:
    type: knn
    params:
      k: 3
  prot_atom_to_lig:
    type: radius
    params:
      r: 8
```

This creates builders accessible as:
```python
builders = get_edge_builders(graph_config)
lig_to_pharm_builder = builders["lig_to_pharm"]  # knn with k=3
prot_atom_to_lig_builder = builders["prot_atom_to_lig"]  # radius with r=8
```

Sources: [omtra/data/graph/edge_factory.py:1-32](), [configs/graph/default.yaml:1-80]()

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Config["Graph Configuration"]
        YAML["graph_config.yaml<br/>edges:<br/>  lig_to_pharm:<br/>    type: knn<br/>    params: {k: 3}"]
    end
    
    subgraph Factory["Edge Builder Factory"]
        GEB["get_edge_builders(graph_config)"]
        REG["edge_builder_register<br/>{knn: hetero_knn,<br/>radius: hetero_radius,<br/>complete: complete_graph}"]
        PARTIAL["functools.partial()<br/>Bind parameters"]
    end
    
    subgraph Builders["Parameterized Builders"]
        B1["lig_to_pharm_builder<br/>= partial(hetero_knn, k=3)"]
        B2["prot_atom_to_lig_builder<br/>= partial(hetero_radius, r=8)"]
        B3["lig_to_lig_builder<br/>= complete_graph"]
    end
    
    subgraph Usage["Runtime Usage"]
        POS["Node positions<br/>x_t, batch_idx"]
        CALL["builder(src_pos, dst_pos,<br/>src_batch_idx, dst_batch_idx)"]
        EDG["Edge indices<br/>tensor[2, n_edges]"]
    end
    
    YAML --> GEB
    GEB --> REG
    REG --> PARTIAL
    PARTIAL --> B1
    PARTIAL --> B2
    PARTIAL --> B3
    
    B1 --> CALL
    POS --> CALL
    CALL --> EDG
    
    style GEB fill:#f9f9f9
    style PARTIAL fill:#f9f9f9
```

Sources: [omtra/data/graph/edge_factory.py:1-32](), [omtra/data/graph/register.py:1-11]()

---

### Edge Count Approximation

#### `approx_n_edges`

Estimates the number of edges for memory allocation and batching purposes.

**Signature:**
```python
def approx_n_edges(
    etype: str, 
    graph_config: DictConfig, 
    num_nodes_dict: Dict[str, int]
) -> Union[int, torch.Tensor]
```

**Approximation Logic:**

| Edge Type | Formula |
|-----------|---------|
| `complete` | `n_src * (n_src - 1)` |
| `knn` | `n_src * k` |
| `radius` | Uses learned MLP approximator |

For radius graphs, the system uses pre-trained MLPs [omtra/data/graph/\_\_init\_\_.py:206-209]() that predict edge counts based on `(radius, n_src, n_dst)`.

Sources: [omtra/data/graph/\_\_init\_\_.py:157-209]()

---

## Prior Sampling API

### Prior Distribution Functions

Prior functions generate initial states (`x_0`) for modalities during training and inference. They are registered using decorators.

#### Registration Decorators

```python
@register_train_prior(name: str)  # For training mode
@register_inference_prior(name: str)  # For inference mode
```

#### Built-in Prior Functions

**Gaussian Priors:**

```python
@register_train_prior("gaussian")
def gaussian_train(
    x1: torch.Tensor,  # Target data
    std: float = 1.0,
    ot: bool = False,  # Optimal transport alignment
    rigid_body: bool = True,
    permutation: bool = True,
    translation: bool = False,
    offset_std: float = 0.0
) -> torch.Tensor

@register_inference_prior("gaussian")
def gaussian_inference(
    n: int,  # Number of samples
    d: Union[int, List[int]],  # Dimensions
    std: float = 1.0,
    **kwargs
) -> torch.Tensor
```

**Key Parameters:**
- `ot=True`: Align `x_0` to `x_1` using optimal transport (during training)
- `translation=True`: Match center of mass to `x_1`
- `offset_std > 0`: Add random offset to center of mass

**Masked CTMC Prior:**

```python
@register_train_prior("masked")
def ctmc_masked_train(
    x1: torch.Tensor,
    n_categories: int
) -> torch.Tensor

@register_inference_prior("masked")
def ctmc_masked_inference(
    n: int,
    d: int  # Number of categories
) -> torch.Tensor
```

Returns all samples as the mask token (index `d`).

**Target-Dependent Prior:**

```python
@register_train_prior("target_dependent_gaussian")
@register_inference_prior("target_dependent_gaussian")
def target_dependent_gaussian_prior(
    x1: torch.Tensor,
    std: float = 1.0
) -> torch.Tensor
```

Returns `x_1 + noise`, useful for denoising tasks.

**Apo Structure Priors:**

```python
@register_train_prior("apo_exp")
@register_inference_prior("apo_exp")
def exp_prior(
    x0: torch.Tensor,  # Experimental apo structure
    std: float = 1.0
) -> torch.Tensor

@register_train_prior("apo_pred")
@register_inference_prior("apo_pred")
def pred_prior(
    x0: torch.Tensor,  # Predicted apo structure
    std: float = 1.0
) -> torch.Tensor
```

Sources: [omtra/priors/priors.py:1-102]()

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Registers["Prior Registries"]
        TR["train_prior_register<br/>{gaussian: gaussian_train,<br/>masked: ctmc_masked_train,<br/>...}"]
        IR["inference_prior_register<br/>{gaussian: gaussian_inference,<br/>masked: ctmc_masked_inference,<br/>...}"]
    end
    
    subgraph PriorTypes["Prior Function Types"]
        G["gaussian<br/>Sample from N(0, std²)"]
        M["masked<br/>All samples = mask_token"]
        TD["target_dependent_gaussian<br/>x_1 + noise"]
        AE["apo_exp<br/>Experimental structure + noise"]
        AP["apo_pred<br/>Predicted structure + noise"]
    end
    
    subgraph Modes["Operating Mode"]
        Train["Training<br/>Has access to x_1"]
        Infer["Inference<br/>No x_1 available"]
    end
    
    Train --> TR
    Infer --> IR
    
    TR --> G
    TR --> M
    TR --> TD
    TR --> AE
    TR --> AP
    
    IR --> G
    IR --> M
    IR --> TD
    IR --> AE
    IR --> AP
    
    style TR fill:#f9f9f9
    style IR fill:#f9f9f9
```

Sources: [omtra/priors/priors.py:1-102](), [omtra/priors/register.py]()

---

### Prior Factory

#### `get_prior`

Factory function that retrieves and configures prior functions for all modalities in a task.

**Signature:**
```python
def get_prior(
    task_cls: Task, 
    config_prior: DictConfig = None, 
    training: bool = False
) -> Dict[str, Tuple[str, Callable]]
```

**Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `task_cls` | `Task` | Task class defining modalities |
| `config_prior` | `DictConfig` | Optional configuration override |
| `training` | `bool` | If `True`, use training priors; else inference priors |

**Returns:** Dictionary mapping modality names to `(prior_name, prior_function)` tuples

**Configuration Lookup:**

1. Check `config_prior[task_name][modality_name]` (if provided)
2. Fall back to `task_cls.priors[modality_name]`

**Example:**

```python
task = DeNovoLigand()
prior_fns = get_prior(task, config_prior=None, training=True)
# Returns:
# {
#   'lig_x': ('gaussian', partial(gaussian_train, std=1.0, ot=True)),
#   'lig_a': ('masked', partial(ctmc_masked_train)),
#   ...
# }
```

Sources: [omtra/priors/prior_factory.py:1-34]()

---

### Sampling Priors on Graphs

#### `sample_priors`

Main function for sampling prior values and attaching them to graph nodes/edges.

**Signature:**
```python
def sample_priors(
    g: dgl.DGLHeteroGraph, 
    task_class: Task, 
    prior_fns: dict,  # Output from get_prior()
    training: bool, 
    com: torch.Tensor = None,  # Center of mass for inference
    fake_atoms: bool = False
) -> dgl.DGLHeteroGraph
```

**Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `g` | `dgl.DGLHeteroGraph` | Graph to add priors to |
| `task_class` | `Task` | Task defining modalities |
| `prior_fns` | `dict` | Prior functions from `get_prior()` |
| `training` | `bool` | Training vs inference mode |
| `com` | `torch.Tensor` | Target center of mass `[batch_size, 3]` (inference only) |
| `fake_atoms` | `bool` | Add extra category for fake atoms |

**Behavior:**

1. **For each modality in `prior_fns`:**
   - Skip if entity not present in graph [omtra/priors/sample.py:25-28]()
   - Determine argument structure based on prior type [omtra/priors/sample.py:48-66]()
   - Call prior function and store result as `{data_key}_0` [omtra/priors/sample.py:69-79]()

2. **Edge symmetry enforcement:**
   - For `lig_to_lig` edges, ensure upper/lower triangle consistency [omtra/priors/sample.py:74-76]()

3. **Center of mass adjustments:**
   - Training: If both ligand and pharmacophore are generated, align their COMs [omtra/priors/sample.py:87-97]()
   - Inference: Move generated entities to specified `com` [omtra/priors/sample.py:99-111]()

**Data Key Mapping:**

| Modality Type | `data_key` | Storage Location | Prior Dimensions |
|---------------|------------|------------------|------------------|
| Position | `x` | `g.nodes[ntype].data['x_0']` | `[n, 3]` |
| Atom type | `a` | `g.nodes[ntype].data['a_0']` | `[n]` (categorical) |
| Charge | `c` | `g.nodes[ntype].data['c_0']` | `[n]` (categorical) |
| Bond order | `e` | `g.edges[etype].data['e_0']` | `[n]` (categorical) |
| Vectors | `v` | `g.nodes[ntype].data['v_0']` | `[n, 4, 3]` |

Sources: [omtra/priors/sample.py:10-113]()

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Input["Input"]
        G["Graph g<br/>with x_1_true data"]
        T["task_class<br/>defines modalities"]
        PF["prior_fns<br/>from get_prior()"]
        MODE["training: bool"]
        COM["com: Tensor<br/>(inference only)"]
    end
    
    subgraph Iteration["For each modality"]
        CHECK["Check if entity<br/>exists in graph"]
        ARGS["Determine args:<br/>- Training: x_1_true<br/>- Inference: n, d"]
        CALL["Call prior_fn(*args)"]
        STORE["Store as x_0 or a_0<br/>in g.nodes/edges.data"]
    end
    
    subgraph PostProcess["Post-Processing"]
        SYM["Enforce symmetry<br/>for lig_to_lig edges"]
        ALIGN["Align COMs:<br/>- Train: pharm→lig<br/>- Infer: all→com"]
    end
    
    subgraph Output["Output"]
        GOUT["Graph g<br/>with x_0, a_0, c_0, e_0<br/>ready for generation"]
    end
    
    G --> CHECK
    T --> CHECK
    PF --> ARGS
    MODE --> ARGS
    CHECK --> ARGS
    ARGS --> CALL
    CALL --> STORE
    STORE --> SYM
    SYM --> ALIGN
    COM --> ALIGN
    ALIGN --> GOUT
    
    style CALL fill:#f9f9f9
    style STORE fill:#f9f9f9
    style ALIGN fill:#f9f9f9
```

Sources: [omtra/priors/sample.py:10-113]()

### Edge Builder Types

| Type | Use Case | Configuration Example |
|------|----------|----------------------|
| `complete` | Fully connected same-type nodes | `type: complete` |
| `knn` | K-nearest spatial neighbors | `type: knn`<br/>`params: {k: 5}` |
| `radius` | All neighbors within distance | `type: radius`<br/>`params: {r: 8.0}` |
| `symmetric` | Inverse of another edge type | Declared in `symmetric_etypes` |

Sources: [omtra/data/graph/edge_builders.py:1-32](), [configs/graph/default.yaml:1-80]()
